findings.where: 'reload' pop-up at x410-445,y535, clipped by the controls list
findings.what: A world 'reload' tag is cut off to 'load' by the controls panel drawn over it. It is a visible overlap and a clear craft bug.
findings.fix: Draw the controls list below world tags, or move the list 24px away from the player-side prompt zone. Keep every in-world tag clear of panel edges by at least 8px.

findings.where: left-side stack: 'current pillager bots' panel and the controls list
findings.what: Two dark panels have different paddings and header sizes. The scoreboard text is small (about 14-15px) with 'dead' values in dim grey that fall under the 4.5:1 contrast floor. The header 'current pillager bots 0' is unclear. The caret icon is small.
findings.fix: Use one 16px label size with 16px padding on both panels, and raise the muted text to --tx-2 #aaa498. Rename the header to 'bots 0'. Make the caret at least 16px.

findings.what: All nine slots are the same weight. The selected slot 3 (blue border, rifle) is hard to tell from slot 1, which has an amber border and is brighter, so two slots look selected. Slot numbers are about 12px, below the 14px floor. The slot tiles are dim, so unselected weapons are hard to read.
findings.fix: Give only the active slot a lime --acc 3px border and a raised --ui-raised fill. Give the other slots a --ui-line-hi border. Raise slot numbers to 16px. Raise unselected icon opacity to at least 0.6. Show slot 1's amber only if it means P1, never selection.

findings.what: '2 / 60' is the hero number and it is red, which is correct for low ammo. But 'auto rifle' and 'view backpack  3 items $1,620' are small and tight against the panel edge, and the '60' is the same size as the '2' with no weight contrast. The panel corner and border are inconsistent with the other panels.
findings.fix: Make the current count 56px weight 800 and the reserve 32px weight 600 in tx-2. Pad the panel to 16px. Use a 4px radius and a 1px --ui-line-hi border to match the other panels.

findings.where: status chips 'concealed' and 'in cover', bottom left (x25-330, y940-980)
findings.what: The two chips use a different shape and colour: amber outline for concealed, teal outline for in cover. They are bigger than the label scale (about 22px). Their circular icons are heavy next to the thin hp bar. They sit close to the hp bar, which is tight.
findings.fix: Set chip text to 20px and the chips to the same height and 4px radius. Use --warn for concealed and --extract for cover only as a small glyph, and keep text tx-1. Leave 16px between chips and hp bar.

findings.where: top centre: timer '8:59', 'extraction 387m' chip, and top right 'contracts 0/8'
findings.what: The timer is the right size for a hero but sits with a small icon and a teal chip that is a different style from the contracts box. The contracts box is a dark bar with a chevron and no matching border, which is inconsistent with the other panels. 'contracts 0/8' is small.
findings.fix: Use one panel style: 4px radius, 1px --ui-line-hi border, --ui-panel fill, 16px type. Align the contracts box top edge with the timer baseline at y=16 and keep 5% margins.

findings.where: contract hint at bottom centre, 'contract item nearby · gold glow marks the box'
findings.what: This is an explaining sentence, which the owner counts as clutter. It also uses a gold bar and a document icon that look different from the other alerts, and it sits close to the hotbar and the controls list.
findings.fix: Cut it to 'contract item nearby' with the gold 3px bar, 20px type. Drop the 'gold glow marks the box' clause. Place it at the top-centre alert banner, as the guide says every alert goes there only.

v.verdict: This is a cluttered in-raid HUD with a big controls panel, so it reads as an amateur layout, and its type sizes, panel styles and hot colours don't agree with each other or the style guide.

findings.what: The list is fully open and is the largest panel on screen. It covers the map, clips the 'cache' label at its right edge (reads 'h cache'), and holds about 20 rows of key hints. The guide says a career raid folds it to one short line, mid-bottom left, opened with F1. The screenshot is of the player-2 search state after a reload, so the open panel may be intended there. The pad glyphs (lb / rb, ls, rs, d-l / d-r) also appear as plain text boxes at mixed widths.
findings.fix: Fold it to one 16px line mid-bottom left (x 5%, y about 1000) and open it only on F1. If it must stay open, make it at most 280px wide and keep it from overlapping world labels. Give every key chip a fixed height of 24px.

findings.what: Many sizes are in use: the 56px ammo hero, about 28px for hp, concealed and in cover, the contract toast at about 20px, 14px feed text and 14px control rows. The guide allows five sizes, and the hp, status and toast sizes do not match any of them. The feed, controls, contracts and top-right type all sit on different baselines, so nothing looks designed as one system.
findings.fix: Use hero 56, body 20 and label 16 only. Set hp, concealed and in cover to 20px f-cond 600. Raise the 14px feed and controls rows to 16px.

findings.where: colour roles: amber and teal pills, gold-bordered slot 1, extraction teal chip, lime
findings.what: Amber (concealed, the contract toast and the slot 1 border) and teal (in cover) are used as hot fills and borders on the same screen as the green hp bar. A selected weapon slot should be lime, but slot 1 is amber and slot 3 is blue. Slot 1 reads as selected and slot 3 as active, so it is unclear which weapon is actually equipped. Lime does not appear anywhere on this screen.
findings.fix: Mark the equipped slot only with a 2px --acc border and a raised fill. Keep amber (--warn) for the contract toast text only. Make the status pills tx-1 text on a --ui-panel fill with a 1px --ui-line-hi border.

findings.what: It is a flat, saturated green slab with 'hp 100' in a heavy white outline. It is the loudest thing in the lower left. It looks like a template, gives no sign of low health and has no hero treatment. It also sits very close to the screen edge (about 13px from the bottom) against the 5% margin rule.
findings.fix: Make the bar 8px thick, with the 'hp 100' label at 20px in tx-1 above it, and a --ok fill that turns --danger below 30%. Move it to the 5% margin (x 96, bottom 54).

findings.what: The panel is crowded. The header line 'current pillager bots 0' is bold, and the 'you' row is brighter than the bot rows, whose names, amounts and 'dead' tags are all muted. 'dead' sits in the same grey as the amounts, and 'dead' is not shown in --danger. The panel hugs the left edge with 8px of margin, and its chevron is a lone control in the corner.
findings.fix: Move it to the 5% margin (x 96, y 54). Set the amounts in a right-aligned f-cond 16px column and the dead tag in --danger. Rename the header 'bots 0', or drop it if the status duplicates the 'out · dead' line.

findings.what: The card is a wide, nearly empty bar with a thin chevron. It is not aligned with the top-centre clock, the roster panel or the 'keyboard' tag at the top-left, so the three top corners sit at different offsets and heights (y 18, y 143, y 8). It is also close to the screen edge, with about 19px of margin.
findings.fix: Put the card and the roster both on the 5% margin (y 54, x 96 and right 96). Cut the contract card width to fit its content, about 200px.

findings.what: It is an explaining sentence ('contract item nearby · gold glow marks the box') with a thin amber left bar, and it butts against the controls panel and the slot bar. A sentence like this is clutter by the style guide. The 'keyboard' device tag at top-left also floats with no anchor, as a lone debug-looking label.
findings.fix: Shorten it to 'contract item nearby' at 20px with the 3px bar. Give it 24px of clearance from the other panels. Move the device tag into the 16px footer legend, or drop it.

findings.where: weapon bar and ammo card, bottom-centre and bottom-right (x548-1910, y902-1080)
findings.what: The ammo card is the only block that follows the hero rule, 25 / 37 at 56px. Its 'auto rifle' label and the 'view backpack  3 items $1,620' line sit very close to its right edge (about 16px of padding), and the card runs off the screen edge with only 10px of margin. The inactive slots are dim silhouettes with low contrast, and the slot numbers are 14px.
findings.fix: Set the card on the 5% margin and give it 24px of padding. Raise the inactive slot art to 60% opacity and the slot numbers to 16px. Keep the weapon-slot row on the same baseline as the ammo card.

v.verdict: The reload prompt now sits on the player and the controls panel is gone, but the prompt is tiny and the HUD panels still don't match each other.

findings.what: The x glyph and 'reload' label are about 12px, set on a small black chip with a lime x. A player on a couch can't read it at 1080, and the chip overlaps the character's head and crosshair ring. With 2/60 ammo this is the most urgent prompt on screen.
findings.fix: Use 16px f-cond 600 for the label and a 24px lime x cap. Put it on an --ui-panel fill with a 1px --acc border and 4px radius. Move it 32px above the player so it clears the head. Pulse it with the --m-in bounce.

findings.where: top-left 'current pillager bots 0' panel vs top-right 'contracts 0/8' panel vs bottom-right ammo panel
findings.what: The three HUD panels use different treatments. The bots panel has a lime-white border and tight padding, the contracts bar has a different height and a chevron, and the ammo panel has its own fill and padding. Title sizes are mixed and the tiny rows (~14px) are below the 16px floor. The '0' after the title is noise.
findings.fix: Give all three the same --ui-panel fill, 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius and 16px padding. Use a 16px 600 title and 16px rows in --tx-2. Drop the '0' after the title and the 'dead' suffix. Add a 3px amber bar on the 'you' row.

findings.what: A flat saturated green bar with a 'hp 100' label drawn at about 32px in a font that looks bolder and larger than any other HUD text. It is hero-sized, but it sits on a low-value bar and competes with the 56px ammo number. It also sits 24px from the edge and doesn't align with the 48px margin used elsewhere.
findings.fix: Make the bar 12px high in --ok on a --ui-line track. Set '100' to 20px f-cond. Move the left edge to 48px and align the bar with the weapon hotbar baseline. Keep the hero size for the ammo number only.

findings.what: The panel is crowded. The 56px red '2' is correctly the hero number, but 'auto rifle', '/ 60', 'view backpack' and '3 items $1,620' float at different sizes with no baseline grid. The fill is also darker than the bots panel.
findings.fix: Right-align the weapon name at 20px. Put '2 / 60' on one baseline with '/ 60' at 20px --tx-2. Move the footer to one 16px --tx-2 line with a 1px --ui-line divider above it.

findings.what: The slots are almost identical dark tiles. Only slot 3 and slot 1 are distinguished, one by an amber border and one by a blue tint, so which one is equipped is unclear. The slot numbers are about 12px, and 'rb' and '60' are tiny.
findings.fix: Mark the equipped slot with a 2px --acc border. Mark slot 1 only with a lime tint, not an amber border. Set slot numbers and counts to 16px --tx-2. Dim empty slots to 60% opacity.

findings.where: top-centre timer and extraction banner, x893-1030,y12-75
findings.what: '8:59' is a good size, but its sun icon sits in a separate black circle with a red ring. The teal 'extraction 165m' pill and its arrow are small, with the arrow tucked under it, and the stack is slightly off-centre.
findings.fix: Centre the 8:59, icon and pill on one axis at x960. Make the pill 16px with a 4px radius and --extract text. Put the arrow inside the pill, to the left of the text.

findings.where: in-world labels: 'chill row', 'the seal 0%', 'the forge', p1 tag
findings.what: Four label styles are in use: letterspaced grey, blue, amber, and a boxed black tag. None has an outline or shadow, so they get lost on the purple map. 'chill row' is faint at about 20px.
findings.fix: Use one world-label style at 16px f-cond 600 with +.04em tracking and a 2px dark outline. Colour by meaning only: --tx-1 for place names, --extract for objectives, --warn for stations.

findings.what: A full-width 300px bar shows only 'contracts 0/8' with a chevron. It is wasted space in the corner and has less contrast against the busy map than the bots panel. It also lacks the folded-controls hint the earlier review asked for, so a player can't tell how to open the controls list.
findings.fix: Shrink the bar to its content width, about 160px. Add a 16px --tx-2 'f1 controls' hint at left 5%, bottom 160px, so the folded list is discoverable.

v.verdict: The big controls list and the duplicate toast are gone and the ammo card is a strong hero, but the HUD corners still don't match each other and the hp bar, roster panel and bottom-left corner are rough.

findings.what: It is a flat saturated green slab with 'hp 100' in oversized, soft-edged type. It matches no other panel (no --ui-panel fill, no border, no radius) and it is the loudest thing in the corner. Green also competes with --ok and the lime accent. It also sits at a different margin from the weapon bar and the ammo card.
findings.fix: Rebuild it as a --ui-panel plate, 320x40, with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius. Put a 12px fill bar inside it (--ok above 40%, --danger below). Show '100' at 20px f-cond 700 in tx-1 and 'hp' at 16px in tx-2. Align it to x=48, with its baseline on the weapon bar's bottom edge.

findings.what: It is flush at x=8 and nowhere near the 48px margin. The header reads 'current pillager bots 0', which is wordy and the '0' is meaningless. 'dead' sits jammed against the money with no column, in tx-2 at about 14px. The footer '0 out · 3 dead' repeats the rows. The row text is below the 16px minimum.
findings.fix: Move it to x=48, y=48. Rename the header 'raiders' at 16px. Put 'dead' in its own right-hand column in --danger at 16px. Set the rows to 16px with 8px gaps, 'you' in tx-1 and the others in tx-2. Delete the footer line. Use a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 85% --ui-panel.

findings.what: Margins and panel styles are inconsistent. The contracts bar sits at 1603 with an 18px margin, the roster at 8px, the ammo card at 1643 with a 10px margin and the hp bar at 24px. The panel fills, borders and radii differ, and the ammo card's fill is flat black.
findings.fix: Use one HUD panel token everywhere: --ui-panel at 85%, a 1px --ui-line-hi border, a 4px radius, and a 48px margin on all four corners. Bring the contracts, roster, ammo and hp panels onto that grid.

findings.what: It is the right size, but the slot numbers are about 12px and low-contrast. The selected slot 1 uses an amber/gold border where selected should be lime (--acc). The selected slot 3, with the weapon, has only a faint blue tint, so the player can't tell which slot is equipped. The bar also sits only a few pixels from the bottom edge.
findings.fix: Mark the equipped slot with a 2px --acc border and --ui-raised fill. Raise slot numbers to 16px tx-2. Lift the bar to a 24px gap from the bottom. Drop the gold border.

findings.what: 'view backpack' and '3 items $1,620' are small, about 14px, and low-contrast, and the card has no key cap for the backpack action. The weapon name 'auto rifle' floats at the top right with no label. The '25 / 37' hero is good.
findings.fix: Set the footer to 16px tx-2. Add a 24x24 key cap for the backpack key before 'view backpack'. Move 'auto rifle' to 16px tx-2 and align it on the left edge with the footer text.

findings.where: world labels near the player (the seal 0%, chill row, the forge, search cache, p1)
findings.what: There are five label styles. 'chill row' is letter-spaced grey and nearly invisible. 'the seal 0%' is blue, 'the forge' is amber, and 'p1' is a large black-and-amber tag. All are about 14-18px and drawn over busy tiles, with no shadow or plate. The 'x search cache' prompt is small and its key cap is tiny.
findings.fix: Use one world-label style: 16px f-cond 600 in tx-1 on a 60% --ui-void plate with 4px padding. Use accent colour only for the interactive prompt. Make the 'x' key cap 24x24, and make the 'p1' tag 16px in amber on that same plate.

findings.what: The clock, the sun icon and the 'extraction 165m' pill are stacked with three different styles. The pill's teal on near-black is fine, but the 14px clock and its tiny arrow are weak for the one hero element of the top HUD.
findings.fix: Draw the clock at 32px f-cond 700 in tx-1. Set the pill text to 16px. Put the sun icon at the left of the clock, 24px. Keep the pill teal --extract at 1px, and remove the loose arrow.

findings.what: It is a dropdown chevron panel with 16px text and a different border and fill from the roster panel. It is lower in priority than the top HUD but pulls the eye as a bright white bar.
findings.fix: Restyle it to the shared HUD panel at 48px margin, 'contracts 0/8' in tx-2 16px with the count in tx-1. Collapse the chevron into a 16px glyph.

v.verdict: The controls list no longer covers the reload prompt, and the screen reads much cleaner. The hud is still uneven: the reload prompt is tiny, the hotbar has two competing highlights, and the ammo panel's hero number is red.

findings.where: reload prompt at the player (x965-1025, y527-545)
findings.what: The only action prompt on screen is about 12px text in a tiny chip. It sits against the busy player sprite, the ring and the crate, so it is nearly unreadable at 1080 from a couch. It is also the primary prompt for this screen.
findings.fix: Raise it to 16px f-cond 600 with 8px padding on a --ui-panel fill. Put the key cap on a lime --acc fill with --acc-ink text, 20px tall. Move it 16px above the head so it clears the weapon sprite.

findings.what: Slot 1 has an amber border and slot 3 has a blue fill with a blue border. Two different highlights fight, so the active slot is unclear. Slot numbers are about 11px and the idle slots are very dark, so their icons barely read.
findings.fix: One active-state rule: lime --acc 3px border plus --ui-raised fill on the active slot only. Every other slot gets a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Raise slot numbers to 16px and idle icons to opacity 0.6 or more. Keep amber only if it means P1, and then not on the slot border.

findings.what: The current count '2' is red, which is correct for low ammo, but 'auto rifle', 'view backpack' and '3 items $1,620' are small and spread over the corners. The panel is also not aligned with the hotbar: its top sits 47px higher than the hotbar and its bottom 8px lower.
findings.fix: Make the count 56px 800 and the '/ 60' 32px 600 in --tx-2. Set the three small lines to 16px --tx-2. Pad the panel 16px and use a 4px radius. Align its top and bottom edges to the hotbar (y950-1060).

findings.where: left stack: bots panel (x8-367, y143-260), contract toast (x15-410, y776-802)
findings.what: The bots panel's rows are about 14px and their muted text is dim, with prices in an even dimmer tint. The header text is 16px but the rows are smaller. The contract toast is two sizes of text with a mid-dot, and 'gold glow marks the box' is an explaining sentence.
findings.fix: Set all bots rows to 16px --tx-2 at 4.5:1 or better, with the header 16px tx-1. Cut the toast to 'contract item nearby' and delete the explaining half. Give both panels the same 4px radius and 16px padding.

findings.what: A full-width saturated green bar carries 'hp 100' at about 32px, sitting at the screen edge with no panel. It is the loudest element in the corner. It crowds the hotbar's left edge and sits only 12px from the bottom, so it breaks the 5% margin.
findings.fix: Shrink the bar to 240px wide and 24px tall. Put 'hp 100' at 20px f-cond 700 in tx-1. Inset it 48px from the left and 32px from the bottom, and use --ok for the fill only.

findings.where: top centre: clock 8:59, 'extraction 165m' chip, 'chill row' label
findings.what: 'chill row' is wide-tracked, grey on a busy world and nearly invisible. The extraction chip is small and teal on dark. The clock and the contracts dropdown at the top right use different sizes and panel styles.
findings.fix: Draw 'chill row' at 20px tx-1 with a 2px dark shadow, no wide tracking. Bring the extraction chip to 16px with 8px padding. Match the contracts panel to the bots panel: same fill, 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius.

findings.where: top-left 'keyboard' tag (x10-105, y6-32) and 'p2' tag (x940-980, y612-642)
findings.what: The 'keyboard' tag uses a monospace face, which the guide bans outside tables. 'p2' is a hard cyan box in a different style from the other tags, and it is 20px but sits on top of the forge.
findings.fix: Put 'keyboard' in f-cond 600 16px in a --ui-panel chip with a 4px radius. Restyle the 'p2' tag as a 24px chip with a 1px cyan border and no fill, and move it 16px above the player's head.

findings.what: They use a fourth text treatment, with a mix of amber and cyan colours and no outline. They are about 16px, low contrast against the purple floor, and 'the forge' overlaps the p2 tag.
findings.fix: Use one world-label style: 16px f-cond 600 tx-1 with a 2px shadow. Colour only a small leading dot. Keep 8px clear of other tags.

v.verdict: The controls list is gone, the pills are quieter and the screen is much cleaner, but the hud still sits tight to the screen edges, uses a mix of off-scale type sizes, and mixes amber, gold, lime and teal accents.

findings.what: The bar is a flat 32px green slab with a 'hp 100' label drawn inside it. It sits 13px from the bottom edge, so it looks pasted on, and it crowds the weapon bar. The green fill is bright, and the label is dark-on-green in a heavy condensed face.
findings.fix: Make the bar 8px thick with a --ok fill that turns --danger below 30%. Put the 'hp 100' label above it at 20px f-cond 600 in tx-1. Move it to x 96, bottom 54 (the 5% margin), with a 1px --ui-line-hi track.

findings.where: top-left roster panel (x8-367, y143-260) and keyboard chip (x10-105, y8-31)
findings.what: The roster panel sits 8px from the edge, with 14px type and a chevron. The header 'current pillager bots 0' is bold, so it competes with the rows, and 'dead' is the same grey as the amounts. The 'keyboard' chip has a lime-green border and green text and a different corner radius from the panels.
findings.fix: Move the panel to x 96, y 54 and the chip to the same margin. Set the rows at 16px, right-align the amounts, and colour 'dead' --danger. Set the header at 16px tx-2. Use a 4px radius and a 1px --ui-line-hi border on all of them.

findings.what: Slot 1 has a gold border and slot 3 has a blue border and a lighter fill, so two slots look selected. Slots 2 and 4-9 are dim and their icons are almost unreadable. The tiny 14px slot numbers are low contrast.
findings.fix: Mark only the equipped slot, with a 2px --acc border and a --ui-raised fill, and give the rest a 1px --ui-line border. Raise the icon opacity on idle slots to about 60%. Set the numbers to 16px tx-2.

findings.where: colour roles: contract toast (x15-410, y776-802), extraction pill (x893-1028, y47-73), 'the forge' label, p2 tag
findings.what: Amber, gold, teal, lime and cyan appear at once in small pills and labels. The 'x' prompt chip is lime on a dark pill, 'the forge' is amber, 'the seal' is blue, 'p2' is a cyan outline box, and the contract toast has an amber bar. They compete for attention and the guide says each colour has one role.
findings.fix: Keep teal only for extraction. Make the 'x' chip --acc, which means interact. Set world labels to tx-1 at 16px. Use --warn only for the contract toast bar. Give the p2 tag a 1px cyan border with tx-1 text.

findings.what: The 56px-class '25 / 37' is a good hero number. But the panel hugs the right edge (10px) and bottom, and it has three text sizes of 14-16px under the name. 'view backpack' and '3 items $1,620' are small and dim.
findings.fix: Move it to right 96, bottom 54. Set 'view backpack' and '3 items $1,620' at 16px in tx-2. Make the weapon name 20px tx-1. Keep 25 at 56px f-cond 800, with 37 at 32px tx-2.

findings.what: The 'contracts 0/8' bar is a wide, empty-looking strip with a chevron, hugging the corner. It is a different width from the left roster panel and uses a different radius.
findings.fix: Align it to the 96px margin and match the roster panel width of 360px. Use 4px radius and 16px label type, with the count in tx-2.

findings.where: timer and extraction block, top-centre (x893-1030, y10-90)
findings.what: The 8:59 clock is about 28px, which is too small for a hero timer. The teal 'extraction 165m' pill stacks tightly below it, with a small arrow, so the block looks cramped.
findings.fix: Make the timer 56px f-cond 800 only when the extraction is under 60s, otherwise 32px. Add 8px between the clock and the pill. Make the pill text 16px and remove the separate arrow in favour of a chevron inside the pill.

findings.what: The widely letter-spaced grey zone name floats over foliage with no backing, so contrast is poor and its spacing reads as a different type style from every other label.
findings.fix: Use 16px f-cond 600 with +.04em tracking and a 1px dark text shadow. Or drop it, since it only names the area.

v.verdict: The reload prompt is now a clear lime key cap on a dark chip, but the HUD panels still don't match each other and the bottom row is crowded and uneven.

findings.where: top-left bots panel (x8-367,y143-260), top-right contracts (x1603-1900,y18-54), ammo panel (x1643-1910,y903-1062)
findings.what: The three panels use different paddings, title sizes and chevron treatments. The bots panel title carries a stray '0' and the rows carry a redundant 'dead' suffix. The ammo panel is much taller than the others, and its 'view backpack' / '3 items $1,620' footer is tiny and cramped.
findings.fix: Give all three panels --ui-panel fill, a 1px --ui-line-hi border, a 4px radius and 16px padding. Use a 16px f-cond 600 title and 16px --tx-2 rows. Drop the '0' after the title and the 'dead' suffix. Add a 3px amber bar on the 'you' row. Put the ammo footer on one 16px line with a 1px --ui-line divider above it.

findings.what: The hp bar is a loud saturated green block with a heavy 'hp 100' label. It is the biggest solid fill on screen and it fights the ammo hero number. It sits 24px from the edge while the hotbar and the other panels sit on different margins. It also sits hard against the corner of the screen.
findings.fix: Make the bar 12px high in --ok on a --ui-line track. Set '100' to 20px f-cond 600 above or beside the bar. Move the left edge to 48px and align the baseline with the hotbar bottom (y≈1058).

findings.what: The equipped state is ambiguous. Slot 1 (fist) has the amber border, while slot 3 (the rifle) has a blue fill and the ammo bar. Two highlight treatments compete, and neither is the lime 'selected' colour. Slot numbers and counts are about 12px and dim. Empty slots are nearly as bright as the filled ones.
findings.fix: Mark only the equipped slot with a 2px --acc border and a --ui-raised fill. Remove the amber border and the blue fill. Set slot numbers and counts to 16px --tx-2. Dim unowned slots to 50% opacity.

findings.what: The prompt is much better, with a lime x cap, but the chip is small (about 20px text) and has no border. It sits close to the head and the aim ring, and the aim ring crowds the 'x'. At 1080 from a couch it still reads as a world label, not an action prompt.
findings.fix: Use 20px f-cond 700 text and a 1px --acc border on a --ui-panel fill. Move it 32px above the head. Give it an --m-in bounce on appear.

findings.where: world labels 'chill row' / 'the forge' (x900-1015,y160-205) and 'p1' tag (x940-980,y612-642)
findings.what: 'chill row' is letter-spaced wide, grey and low contrast on the purple ground. 'the forge' is amber, which reads as the accent and the warn colour at once. The 'p1' tag is a solid amber block that is heavier than the reload prompt and looks like a button.
findings.fix: Set 'chill row' to 16px --tx-1 at +.04em with a 60% black text shadow. Make 'the forge' --tx-2. Make the p1 tag a 16px label on a --ui-panel chip with a 2px amber bottom bar rather than a solid fill.

findings.what: The teal chip is correct for extraction but is a different size and shape from the other panels. The small teal arrow under it (y≈83) floats with no connection.
findings.fix: Use 16px f-cond 600 text in --extract on a --ui-panel fill with a 1px --extract border and a 4px radius. Attach the arrow 8px below, or drop it.

findings.where: scene tint, the whole right half
findings.what: The purple wash lowers contrast across the right half. Walls and floor read as a single mauve mass, and the HUD text there (contracts, ammo) sits on a mixed background.
findings.fix: Keep the --ui-panel opacity at 90% or higher on the right-hand panels. Reduce the purple overlay alpha to 0.15 around the HUD edges.

v.verdict: The HUD is readable, but the earlier corner-panel advice was mostly not followed: the hp bar is still a bare green slab, the roster sits off the grid, and the weapon bar's gold border and selection are still muddled.

findings.what: It is still a flat, saturated green slab. The 'hp 100' text sits inside it in a different, larger type than the rest of the HUD. It is jammed against the bottom-left corner, 24px from the left and about 13px from the bottom. It does not use the panel language, and it falls on the weapon bar's baseline only by accident.
findings.fix: Rebuild it as a 320x40 --ui-panel plate with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius. Inside it, put a 12px --ok fill bar (--danger below 40%). Set '100' at 20px f-cond 700 in tx-1 and 'hp' at 16px in tx-2. Place it at x=48, with its bottom at 1032 (48px margin).

findings.what: It sits 8px from the left edge and floats at y=143, so it is off every margin. The 'current pillager bots 0' header is confusing. The 'dead' tags are glued to the dollar figures in tx-2 instead of sitting in their own column. Row text is about 14px, below the 16px floor. The footer line '0 out · 3 dead' repeats information the rows already show.
findings.fix: Move it to x=48, y=48. Rename the header 'raiders' at 16px. Put 'dead' in its own right-hand column in --danger at 16px. Set the rows to 16px with 8px gaps, 'you' in tx-1 and the others in tx-2. Delete the footer line. Use a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 85% --ui-panel.

findings.what: The four corner blocks use four different edges and margins: contracts at about 18px, roster at 8px, hp at 24px, ammo at about 10px. They also have four different treatments (a dropdown, a dark card, a green bar, a bordered card). The HUD reads as unrelated parts.
findings.fix: Use one HUD panel token: --ui-panel at 85%, a 1px --ui-line-hi border, a 4px radius, and a 48px margin on all four corners. Align the contracts and ammo panels' outer edges to x=1872, and the hp and roster panels' outer edges to x=48.

findings.what: Slot 1 (fist) has a gold border and slot 3 (auto rifle) has a blue-tinted fill, so two slots look selected. Slot numbers are about 12px and barely readable. The bar sits only 20px above the bottom. The empty slots are dim, which is fine, but the lime accent is not used for selection at all.
findings.fix: Mark only the equipped slot, with a 2px --acc border and --ui-raised fill. Remove the gold border from slot 1 and the blue tint from slot 3, which holds the rifle but is not equipped. Raise the slot numbers to 16px tx-2. Lift the bar to a 24px gap from the bottom.

findings.what: The '25 / 37' hero number is correctly the biggest thing in the corner, but the footer 'view backpack' and '3 items $1,620' are about 14px with no key cap. The card is only about 10px from the screen edge. 'auto rifle' is right-aligned while the footer is left-aligned, so the edges do not line up.
findings.fix: Set the footer to 16px tx-2. Add a 24x24 key cap for the backpack key before 'view backpack'. Move 'auto rifle' to 16px tx-2 and align it on the left edge with the footer text. Move the card to a 48px margin.

findings.what: The timer is about 28px, below the 56px hero size. The teal pill is a different shape from every other panel. The 'chill row' zone label below uses wide letter-spacing and a different face, and 'the forge' in amber sits as a floating, unframed label.
findings.fix: Set the timer at 32px f-cond 700 tx-1 (or the 56px hero if it is the one hero). Put the extraction line in a 4px-radius --ui-panel plate with a 1px --extract border. Set the zone label at 16px tx-2 with the default tracking of +.04em.

findings.what: It is a boxed dropdown with a chevron, a different component from the roster card, which has a similar chevron but different padding and border. It is cramped against the top edge, about 19px.
findings.fix: Use the same panel token and header height as the roster (a 40px header row, 16px label, 16px padding), and place it at x=1872 right edge, y=48. Use the same chevron glyph in tx-2 for both.

findings.what: The prompt has the right key cap and sits close to the player, which is good. But the pill is a rounded black chip with a yellow cap, and it matches no panel style. The 'p1' tag below it is a boxed amber label whose style is also its own.
findings.fix: Give the prompt a 4px-radius --ui-panel fill with a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Make the key cap a 24x24 --acc fill with --acc-ink text. Keep 'p1' amber but give it the same 4px radius and a 16px f-cond label.

v.verdict: The reload prompt is now a proper lime-capped chip above the player and reads clearly, but the HUD around it is still inconsistent: the ammo count is red and mismatched, the hotbar has two competing highlights, the hp bar is oversized, and the contracts and bots panels differ.

findings.what: Slot 1 has an amber border and slot 3 a blue fill, so two slots look active. Idle weapon icons are near-black and slot numbers are tiny. The 'rb' tag in slot 1 is cramped at about 11px.
findings.fix: Use one active rule: a 3px --acc border on the equipped slot with a --ui-raised fill. Every other slot gets a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Raise idle icons to opacity 0.6 or more and slot numbers to 16px --tx-2. Drop the blue fill and the amber border. Make the 'rb' tag 16px or move it out of the slot.

findings.what: The 2 is red --danger at roughly 56px with '/ 60' in white. Red means the magazine is low or empty, but this is just a reload cue, so the colour is a false alarm and conflicts with the lime scheme. 'view backpack' and '3 items $1,620' are about 14px and crowded at the bottom. The panel top (y903) does not align with the hotbar top (y950).
findings.fix: Use --tx-1 for the count and turn it --danger only at 25% ammo or less. Set '/ 60' to 32px --tx-2. Set the footer lines to 16px --tx-2 with 16px padding. Align the panel's bottom edge to the hotbar's (y1060) and give it a 4px radius.

findings.what: A flat, wide green slab with a 'hp 100' label that is too large and clipped by the bar edges. It sits only 12px from the screen edge, below the 5% margin, and crowds the hotbar's left side. It is also the heaviest HUD element, outweighing the ammo.
findings.fix: Shrink the bar to 240x20px with a --ok fill on a --ui-void track. Set the 'hp 100' label to 20px f-cond 700 in --tx-1, placed beside the bar rather than inside it. Inset the group 48px from the left and 32px from the bottom.

findings.what: Text is about 14-15px and --tx-2 on a near-black fill. The dead rows are dim, and '$2,925 dead' mixes a value with a status word. The panel sits 8px from the edge and has no consistent padding.
findings.fix: Use 16px rows with a 16px header in --tx-1. Show the status as a small --danger glyph instead of the word 'dead'. Pad the panel 16px, set the radius to 4px and inset it 48px from the left.

findings.what: The chip uses a different fill, border and radius from the bots panel and the ammo block, so three panel styles sit on one screen. The chevron is faint.
findings.fix: Use the --ui-panel fill, a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius on all three. Set the label to 16px f-cond 600. Align it to the 48px right margin.

findings.what: The 8:59 timer is about 28px, below the 56px hero size, and 'extraction 162m' is in teal in a pill with an arrow floating beneath. The zone title 'chill row' / 'the forge' at x900-1015 uses wide letter-spacing in a different style, and the yellow subtitle is a third accent treatment.
findings.fix: Make the timer 32px f-cond 700 in --tx-1. Keep the teal extraction pill at 16px with the arrow inside it. Set the zone title to 20px f-cond 600 with +.04em tracking and the subtitle in --tx-2, not yellow.

findings.what: The chip is good. The lime x-cap on a dark fill follows the guide. The label is about 18px and sits tight against the key cap, with only 8px between them. The chip is 20px above the head and just clears the aim ring.
findings.fix: Set the label to 16px f-cond 600 and pad the chip 8px. Raise the chip 8px more so the aim ring never touches it. Keep the lime cap.

findings.what: The p2 tag is a cyan box with a pole below the player. It is correct for P2 but reads like a debug marker. The pole line is thin and floats.
findings.fix: Make it a 16px label chip with a 4px radius and a 1px cyan border on --ui-panel. Attach it directly under the feet with an 8px gap and drop the pole.

v.verdict: The in-raid HUD is readable and the 25/37 ammo number leads, but none of the earlier advice was applied: the hud still has no shared margin, three competing highlights on the weapon bar, and mixed colour roles.

findings.what: Slot 1 (amber border) and slot 3 (blue fill) are both highlighted, so it is unclear which weapon is equipped. Idle slots are too dark, and the amber on slot 1 competes with the lime accent and with P1/P2 colour meaning.
findings.fix: Mark only the equipped slot, with a 2px --acc border and a --ui-raised fill. Give every other slot a 1px --ui-line border. Raise idle icon opacity to about 60%. Set the slot numbers to 16px tx-2.

findings.what: The bar is a flat, thick, saturated green slab with a 36px condensed 'hp 100' label inside it. It sits 13px from the screen edge, off the margin. The label is one of the loudest things on screen, louder than the ammo hero number, and is partly clipped by the bar edge.
findings.fix: Make the bar 8px thick with a --ok fill that turns --danger below 30%, on a 1px --ui-line-hi track. Put 'hp 100' above it at 20px f-cond 600 tx-1. Place the block at x 96, bottom 54.

findings.where: HUD margins: keyboard chip (x10-105, y8-31), roster panel (x8-367, y143-260), contracts (x1602-1900, y18-54), ammo panel (x1642-1910)
findings.what: Each element sits 8-18px from the edge, so there is no shared safe margin. The corners look ragged, and on a TV some of it will be cut off. The panels also use inconsistent radii and border weights.
findings.fix: Put all corner elements on the 5% margin: left 96, top 54, right 96, bottom 54. Use a 4px radius and a 1px --ui-line-hi border on every panel and chip.

findings.what: The rows are tiny, about 14px. The header and the 'you' row have the same weight as the rows below them. 'dead' is grey, not --danger. The panel hangs far below the top-left corner, away from its related chip.
findings.fix: Set the rows at 16px, right-align the amounts, and colour 'dead' --danger. Make the header 16px tx-2 and the 'you' row tx-1 at weight 700. Anchor the panel at x 96, y 54 and move the chip into the same stack.

findings.where: colour roles: extraction pill (x893-1028, y47-73), contract toast (x15-410, y776-802), 'the forge' label (x949-1010, y185-202), 'x search cache' chip, p2 tag (x940-980, y612-642)
findings.what: Teal, amber, yellow-orange and lime are all used for small labels with no clear rule. 'the forge' is amber, which suggests a warning. The 'x' chip is lime, which is correct. The p2 tag is a cyan box with an off-weight font. The 'chill row' district label uses wide letter-spacing that matches nothing else.
findings.fix: Keep teal only for extraction. Make world labels tx-1 at 16px f-cond 600. Use --warn only for the contract toast bar. Give the p2 tag a 1px cyan border with tx-1 text. Set 'chill row' in 16px f-cond with +.04em tracking.

findings.what: The 25 / 37 hero number is good, but 'view backpack' and '3 items $1,620' are 14px and dim, and the panel is flush to the edge. The weapon name 'auto rifle' sits top-right and is small against the 56px number.
findings.fix: Move the panel to right 96, bottom 54. Set 'view backpack' and '3 items $1,620' at 16px tx-2. Make 'auto rifle' 20px tx-1. Keep 25 at 56px f-cond 800 and 37 at 32px tx-2.

findings.what: The 8:59 timer is 28px with a sun icon, with the extraction pill and a small teal arrow stacked tightly under it. They crowd one another and the timer is smaller than the 56px hero size.
findings.fix: Set the timer at 32px f-cond 700. Leave 8px between the timer and the pill, and 16px between the pill and the arrow.

findings.what: The panel is a full-width box with a chevron but no icon or progress. The chevron is crammed against the edge, and the panel is not aligned with the ammo panel below it.
findings.fix: Right-align it to right 96 and give it a 16px side pad. Use a 16px chevron in tx-2 and set the 0/8 count in tx-2 at 16px.

v.verdict: A clean, well-aligned how-to-play card with a clear title, tidy key-cap table and a visible lime prompt, but it is held back by a ghosted underlay that shows through the scrim, a stray lime bar on the card edge, and a redundant close button on a walk-up screen.

findings.where: scrim behind the card (header area around y=200-230 and the middle y=380-400)
findings.what: Ghost text from the underlying HUD ('a shoot/...' and '[x] to ...' blurred lines) bleeds through the card at roughly 8% opacity beside the title and in the table. It reads as dirty overlap, and the card fill looks semi-transparent instead of the solid --ui-panel.
findings.fix: Make the card fill opaque #16191b. Raise the scrim to rgba(6,7,8,.80) and blur the layer behind it, or hide the underlying HUD prompt layer while this card is open.

findings.where: HUD behind the card (team score, extraction tag, player 2 bar, hp/armour, weapon slots, riot scattergun 7/42)
findings.what: The scrim is too weak and the blur is too light. Hero numbers like '7 / 42' and '0 sp' are still bright, and they compete with the card, so the eye splits between the card and the HUD. The 'join your team · team score 0 sp' line in lime at the bottom sits outside the card and competes with the card's own prompt.
findings.fix: Darken to scrim .80 plus a 6px blur. Drop the lime join-your-team line while the card is open, or fold it into the card footer. Only one lime prompt should be on screen.

findings.what: A short lime tick sits on the card's top border above the title. It is the only accent on the card frame, it is not tied to anything, and it reads as a stray artifact instead of a deliberate focus marker.
findings.fix: Either remove it, or make it a full-width 3px lime top bar on the card, or align it exactly to the title's left edge, inset 0, 32px wide, 3px high, like the other windows.

findings.what: A boxed close button is drawn on a walk-up screen that continues on any key. It is a second, competing action, and its 1px grey border is faint. Its box is 48px square but the glyph is ~12px and looks lost.
findings.fix: If the x is standard for every window card, keep it but enlarge the glyph to 20px and use --ui-line-hi #4a5257 for the border. If this walk-up screen is any-key-only, remove it.

findings.what: The headers are about 14px in dim grey, below the 16px label minimum. They are the key to reading the whole table, and they sit far above the first row with a ~20px gap before the rule.
findings.fix: Use 16px f-cond 600, +.04em, color --tx-2 #aaa498. Tighten the gap to the rule to 8px.

findings.what: Key caps have a thin border with no fill difference, they are ragged in width, and the row labels (move, aim) use the same weight and size as the key caps. There is no separation of label from value, so every row has the same visual weight. The extract row's 'in the ring' hint is ~14px and its teal ring is small and ambiguous.
findings.fix: Set row labels to --tx-2 at 20px 600 and key caps to --tx-1 on --ui-raised #1e2225 with a 4px radius and a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Give every cap a 40px height and 16px side padding. Raise 'in the ring' to 16px.

findings.what: 'player 1: press any key' is right-aligned and sits close to the card's bottom edge (about 50px). The lime ring bullet and the 20px text are readable, but the prompt is smaller than the title, so the primary action is weaker than the heading. It also sits off-centre from the table, whose columns start at the left.
findings.fix: Enlarge it to 24px with the lime ring at 28px. Align it to the controller column's left edge (x=1052) or centre it. Leave 24px of padding below it.

findings.where: background HUD labels ('keyboard' tag top-left, 'pillagers' wordmark, 'f1 controls')
findings.what: The 'keyboard' tag in the top-left is cropped against the screen edge and low contrast. The 'pillagers' wordmark floats unanchored beside it, so the corner looks cluttered even while the modal is open.
findings.fix: Hide the HUD tags and wordmark while the modal is open, or at least give the 'keyboard' tag 24px of screen-edge margin.

v.verdict: The raid HUD has too many competing banners stacked in the top centre and the middle, and it breaks the one-place-per-line rule. The overlapping name tag and a stray 'a' in the extract line show it is unfinished.

findings.where: centre of screen, under the player ring
findings.what: The 'sweatlordsupreme' name tag overlaps a cache label (reads '...ache'). The red underline bar collides with the text and the result is unreadable.
findings.fix: Draw only one label at a time. Hide the cache label while a name tag sits within 120px of it. Give the tag a 4px radius --ui-panel plate with 8px padding. Put the cache label on its own line at least 24px below the tag.

findings.what: This line has a stray 'a' and an exclamation mark. It is thin teal text with no plate, drawn on busy terrain, so it is hard to read. It also repeats the 'hold [x] to extract' banner and the 'extraction 3m' chip, which breaks the rule that a line appears in one place.
findings.fix: Remove the stray token. Write it as 'extracting 26s' in 56px f-cond 800 --extract (the hero size, once per screen). Put it on an --ui-panel plate at 80% opacity with 8px padding. Drop the 'hold [x] to extract' banner while extraction is running. Delete the duplicate lines.

findings.where: top-centre stack: team score, extraction 3m chip, teal arrow, siege incoming
findings.what: Four separate elements are stacked in 200px at top centre. The panel edges do not line up: the score panel is about 300px wide, the siege banner about 310px and the chip about 150px. The siege banner sits close to the arrow and score block and has a red border and glow that clash with the teal chips. The alert itself is the right place for an alert, but the cluster crowds it.
findings.fix: Make one 320px column with consistent 8px gaps. Give the score panel, the chip and the banner the same width and a 4px radius. Move the extraction arrow into the chip. Put the siege banner 24px below the column and draw it in --danger with no outer glow.

findings.what: The 56px-class cyan text is the largest thing on screen. It out-shouts the score, the ammo number and the siege alert. Its panel is a translucent teal-grey that does not match the other panels, and the bracketed [x] reads as a debug string.
findings.fix: Use 32px f-cond 700 text on an --ui-panel plate with a 3px --extract bar on the left. Show the key as a 24px keycap chip with a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Hold the scale back for the extraction hero number only.

findings.where: bottom-left: f1 controls, armour 60, hp 100 bars
findings.what: The 'f1 controls' chip floats at x≈410, about 380px from the armour bar, and has no relationship to the left HUD column. The armour bar (about 20px high) and hp bar (about 34px high) have different heights and the labels differ in size. The hp bar's bright green flat fill competes with the lime accent.
findings.fix: Give armour and hp one shared height of 24px, 8px apart, with 16px f-cond 600 labels. Put the hp fill in --ok and the armour fill in a desaturated blue. Align the f1 chip's left edge to the bar edge at x=24 and set it 16px above the armour bar.

findings.what: Eight of the ten slots are empty and dim, with large muted numerals. The two filled slots carry different markers (a lime frame for slot 2, a purple fill for slot 5), so it is not clear which is selected. The ammo panel at bottom right is a different shade and radius from the hotbar, and its 'compact smg' label is body-sized at the top right.
findings.fix: Show only the first N occupied slots, or dim empty slots to 40% opacity with no numeral. Use the lime --acc frame for the selected slot only. Show the other slots' rarity with a 3px bar at the bottom. Give the ammo panel and the hotbar the same --ui-panel fill and 4px radius, and align their bottom edges.

findings.where: '17 hostiles closing in' chip and 'goals 0/3' dropdown
findings.what: The red hostile chip is a thin small box floating at screen centre-bottom with its own border colour, and the goals dropdown at top right looks like a web form control with a chevron. Neither shares a style with the score panel.
findings.fix: Put both on the shared --ui-panel plate with a 4px radius and 1px --ui-line-hi border. Use 16px f-cond 600 labels. Make the hostile count a 16px --danger label with a 3px --danger bar on the left, set 16px above the hotbar and aligned to its centre.

findings.where: player 1 tag at left edge and the weather icon
findings.what: The 'player 1' tag is a small tab stuck to the screen edge, 70px wide and 16px tall, at about 12px from the edge, so it clips the safe margin. The weather icon sits as a round chip beside the score panel with no label or reason.
findings.fix: Keep both inside a 5% safe margin (96px horizontal at 1080p). Make the player tag at least 16px type on a panel plate coloured in the P1 amber bar. Move the weather icon into the top-right group beside goals.

v.verdict: The easy-mode prompt reads clearly, with a lime yes button against a dark card, but the card is oversized for one question. It has dead space, no scrim, and a busy HUD competing around it, and the HUD itself is inconsistent in type size, panel treatment and weight.

findings.what: A one-line question sits in a 935x318 card with about 100px of empty space between the title and the buttons. The card is a flat black rectangle with sharp corners, no border and no x or close affordance, so it matches neither the 4px radius panels nor the centred-card-with-x window rule. The title is only about 32px and the countdown '11' is a tiny grey number in the top-right corner, so the timeout is easy to miss.
findings.fix: Shrink the card to about 640x240 with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius. Put the title at 32px, then 24px of gap, then the buttons. Make the countdown a 16px label with a shrinking lime bar along the card top, replacing the orphaned stub at the top-left (x 493-562).

findings.what: There is no --scrim, so the raid keeps full colour and contrast behind the card. The bright purple and orange map, the teal extract chip, the 'meridian strongbox' label and the enemy tag all compete with the modal. The top HUD and hotbar stay lit as well, so the eye is pulled away from the decision.
findings.fix: Draw a full-screen rgba(6,7,8,.80) scrim under the card. Dim the HUD with it, or keep only the countdown and the player 2 bars above it.

findings.what: Yes is a huge lime slab (406x100), well beyond the guide's one main action, and the 'y' and 'n' key hints are the same 20px weight as the labels, so they read as 'y yes' and 'n no' rather than as key chips. 'no' is a thin-outlined ghost with weak contrast. Neither button shows pad focus, a bounce or a hover state, and the label text is small for a 100px-tall button.
findings.fix: Make the buttons 56px high with 4px radius. Put the key hints in a 16px --tx-2 chip on the left of each button, with the label at 20px f-cond 700. Give 'no' a --ui-line-hi border and --tx-1 text. Give the focused button a 2px --acc outline, and use the lime fill only on the one focused or default button.

findings.what: The team score panel is crowded. 'team score' is tiny, '0 sp' is large, 'you 0 sp' and 'p2 0 sp' are tiny and tight against it, and the menu hamburger floats loose to the right. The timer 9:59 is wedged at the panel's bottom edge and clipped by the teal 'extract 108m' chip, which overlaps the panel's lower border. The panel also touches the top edge of the screen.
findings.fix: Rebuild the panel on the 8px grid: 16px padding, top margin of at least 24px, the 56px hero for the score only and the 20px timer on its own row. Move the extract chip out below the panel with an 8px gap. Set the hamburger inside the panel's right padding, and use 16px minimum for the you/p2 lines.

findings.what: The 'crawler m-64' tag is overprinted by a '15' damage number and a second tag ('player 2'), which makes it illegible. An orange underline and a red tick collide with the text, a 'ld' fragment shows below it, and everything is crammed against the screen edge.
findings.fix: Render one stacked name tag per entity with at least 8px of vertical offset. Suppress the damage number while the tag is shown, or float it 24px above. Clamp tags to at least 5% from the screen edge.

findings.what: The armour and hp bars are different heights, widths and weights (hp is huge, armour is slim), and the labels are left-aligned inside the fills. The 'f1 controls' chip floats unanchored above the hotbar. The 'wall glitch saved to run report' toast is a third panel style with a lime-grey left stub, and a 'player 2 joined' toast sits right above the hotbar. Several panel styles coexist with different fills, radii and borders.
findings.fix: Use one bar height of 24px with 16px labels at the same weight, stacked with an 8px gap. Align 'f1 controls' to the hotbar left edge at the 5% margin. Give both toasts the single --ui-panel fill with a 4px radius and a 1px border, stacked in the left feed only.

findings.what: The ammo panel is sound, with a hero 24 and a muted '/ 144', but the weapon name is tiny against it and the panel sits flush to the right and bottom screen edges, with 12px of margin where the guide asks for 5%. Hotbar slot numbers are tiny (about 14px) and the empty slots are barely visible. The only selected-slot cue is a small amber outline, which is the P1 colour rather than the lime for 'selected'. The hotbar is crowded against the bottom edge.
findings.fix: Inset the ammo panel and hotbar 24px or more from the screen edges. Set slot numbers to 16px --tx-2 and the weapon name to 20px. Make the selected slot a 2px --acc outline, and drop the unfocused slots to 50% opacity.

findings.what: A 'goals 0/3' pill with a chevron looks like an unstyled web select. It uses a different radius and border from the score panel and has no icon or progress cue. The 'keyboard' chip at top-left is another unrelated style, in a monospace font at 16px against a bright map.
findings.fix: Restyle both with the shared --ui-panel fill, a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius, and f-cond 600 at 16-20px. Give goals a 3-segment progress pip instead of the chevron. Move the device chip to the 5% margin, or drop it after the first 5 seconds.

v.verdict: A raid-time easy-mode prompt over the live HUD: the yes/no card is clean and legible, but the lime fill dominates and the HUD around it is crowded, clipped and inconsistent.

findings.where: hud top-right, edge of screen (right edge, y≈380)
findings.what: A pink/lavender 'the lon…' label is clipped off the right edge of the screen, and its colour belongs to no token.
findings.fix: Clamp the label inside the 5% safe margin (≥96px from the right edge) and ellipsize it. Use tx-1 or the player colour, not an ad-hoc lavender.

findings.what: The plate is cramped. 'you 0 sp' and 'p1 0 sp' sit tight against the hero number, the timer is almost touching the bottom edge, and the extract 138m chip butts directly against the plate with no gap. Type sizes are mixed (about 14, 16, 40 and 24px) with no clear hierarchy.
findings.fix: Give the plate 16px padding. Leave 8px between the plate and the extract chip. Set the score to 56 hero, the sub-scores and the label to 16, and the timer to 20. Move the per-player lines onto one row below the hero.

findings.what: The card is flat, with no 4px radius, no border and no scrim over the busy map, so the HUD and map stay at full brightness around it. The 11 countdown at top-right is tiny, floats alone and has no unit. A thin lime tick at the top-left corner reads as a rendering artefact. There is a large dead gap between the title and the buttons.
findings.fix: Apply a scrim of rgba(6,7,8,.80) behind the card, a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius. Make the countdown 32px f-cond in tx-2, or turn it into a bar under the title. Remove the corner tick or make it a full-width 3px progress bar. Reduce the title-to-button gap to 24px.

findings.what: The lime fill is a huge slab (406×100) that out-shouts the title, so boldness goes to the action and the title at once. The key letters 'y' and 'n' sit at the same weight and size as the labels, so the hint does not read as a key hint. The no button has a hairline border with low contrast and no visible pad-focus state.
findings.fix: Shrink the buttons to 64px tall. Render the key hint as a 16px keycap chip to the left of the label. Make the no border --ui-line-hi at 2px. Show focus on the selected button as a 3px lime outline. Fill only the default button.

findings.what: The bars are flat, saturated slabs with large tinted text. The hp bar is much taller than the armour bar. The armour text is hard to read, with white text on pale blue. The 'f1 controls' chip floats above them in an unrelated dark box.
findings.fix: Use one bar height (24px) for both, with 8px between them. Use --acc-ink text on pale fills or tx-1 on dark fills. Align the f1 controls chip to the bar's left edge at the same 5% margin.

findings.where: bottom-centre toast 'in pillager's party' and the air strike bar
findings.what: The toast is a small 14px black box floating at a random position above the weapon bar. It is not aligned to the bar's centre or to anything else. The air strike bar's own text is tiny and its fill is barely visible. The two sit tight against the hotbar.
findings.fix: Dock the toast to the top-centre banner position, or centre it with 16px type and 16px padding. Give the air strike bar a 16px label and a visible track in --ui-line-hi. Keep ≥16px between the stack and the hotbar.

findings.what: The hotbar slots 1 to 8 are all dark and nearly identical, and the digit labels are small at about 14px. The ammo block is a large black rectangle whose bottom edge sits near the screen edge. '25 / 150' is strong, but 'auto rifle' sits at the top-right with generous empty space.
findings.fix: Make the slot numerals 16px tx-2. Set the ammo block bottom to 5% (≥54px) from the screen edge. Use hero 56 for the 25 and 32 for the 150. Left-align 'auto rifle' to the number.

findings.where: top-right goals 0/3 and the left player 1 tag
findings.what: The goals chip is a dark rounded box with a chevron, and the player 1 plate is a rectangle with a thin cyan bar. They share no panel language (radii differ, borders are absent or heavier). 'player 1' is blue/cyan on a world-space label, which contradicts P1 = amber.
findings.fix: Use one 4px-radius panel style with a 1px --ui-line-hi border for both. Recolour the P1 name tag and bar to amber, with cyan reserved for P2.

v.verdict: The easy-mode card and its scrim are gone, so this is now a clean in-raid HUD where the hp, ammo and hotbar read well. The top-centre cluster, the stray 'keyboard' chip and the crowded enemy tag still look unfinished.

findings.what: The panel is flush to the top edge with about 4px of padding. The 'team score' label is tiny, the 'you 0 sp / p2 0 sp' lines are about 14px, and the hamburger floats outside the panel's content edge. The extract chip hangs off the bottom edge and overlaps the panel. A teal arrow sits just under it with no clear link to it.
findings.fix: Set the top margin to 24px and the padding to 16px. Keep the 56px hero for the score only. Put the you/p2 lines at 16px minimum in --tx-2. Move the extract chip 8px below the panel. Tuck the hamburger inside the right padding, and attach the arrow to the chip.

findings.where: enemy tag over the crawler (x 1050-1145, y 440-495)
findings.what: The orange name tag, the white damage number '10', the '!' alert and the enemy sprite are stacked on top of each other. The number sits on the sprite and under the tag, so it is hard to read.
findings.fix: Float the damage number 24px above the tag, or hide it while the tag is shown. Put the '!' 8px above the tag. Show the tag at 16px with 8px of vertical clearance from the sprite.

findings.what: The control looks like a native dropdown. It has a heavy dark fill, a chevron and a different corner radius from the other panels. It does not match the score panel or the ammo card. The 24px margin to the screen edge is also not 5%.
findings.fix: Re-skin it as a --ui-panel card with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius. Use a 16px label and a --tx-2 chevron, and align its top edge to the score panel at y 24. Use the 5% margin on the right.

findings.what: It is a tiny green-tinted chip jammed into the corner with a radius and colour that match nothing else. Its job is unclear and it competes with the HUD for attention.
findings.fix: Fade it out after 3s, or fold it into the player 1 bar as a 16px --tx-2 glyph. Put it on the 8px grid at 24px,24px.

findings.what: The 60/360 hero number is strong and clear. The card is nearly flush to the right and bottom edges, and its 14px-class gap to the hotbar is tighter than the other margins. 'support mg' is the only secondary text and is a bit dim.
findings.fix: Inset the card 5% from the right edge and 24px from the bottom. Set 'support mg' at 20px in --tx-1. Use the same 4px radius and the same border as the score panel.

findings.where: bottom-left hp and armour bars with the 'f1 controls' chip (x 22-535, y 920-1070)
findings.what: The bars sit about 22px from the edge, flush with the screen bottom. The 'f1 controls' chip floats in a dark box with no relationship to either bar, and it is partly hidden behind the hotbar edge.
findings.fix: Lift the bars to a 48px bottom margin and give them a shared 8px gap. Align the chip's left edge to the bars at x 48 and put it 8px above the armour bar. Use a 16px label.

findings.where: 'player 2 joined' toast (x 893-1027, y 893-930) and player 2 bar (x 15-170, y 322-360)
findings.what: The toast is small, sits tight on the hotbar's top edge, and has a different border and fill from the score panel. The player 2 bar in the left margin is a small cyan-tinted slab that is detached from the HUD grid.
findings.fix: Lift the toast 16px above the hotbar and use the shared panel style at 20px. Move the player 2 bar to the left margin at the same x as the hp bar, and use a 16px label.

findings.what: The letter-spaced grey title reads as a UI element but has no panel, low contrast against the purple floor, and a weight that matches nothing in the HUD type scale.
findings.fix: Use f-cond 700 at 32px in --tx-1 at 70% opacity with a fade-out after 4s, or hide it once the run starts.

v.verdict: The easy-mode modal is gone and the HUD is readable, but the score plate still sits flush against the top edge, the left-edge player strip and keyboard chip are cramped, and the bottom row has several unrelated panels with no shared structure.

findings.where: top-centre score plate (team score / 0 sp / you, p1 / 10:00)
findings.what: The plate is flush with the top of the screen (y=0) and has no padding. The 'you 0 sp' and 'p1 0 sp' lines are tiny (~14px) and crammed beside the hero. The 10:00 timer is the same visual weight as the hero. The extract chip touches the plate's bottom edge.
findings.fix: Offset the plate 16px from the top. Use 16px padding all round. Set the hero 'sp' number at 56px f-cond 800. Set the timer at 20px tx-2. Put the 'you' and 'p1' lines in one 16px row below the hero. Leave 8px between the plate and the extract chip.

findings.what: The strip sits against the left edge at 14px, well outside the 5% safe margin (96px). Its lavender name is an ad-hoc colour, and the bars are paper-thin. It also repeats the 'player 1' tag over the character.
findings.fix: Move the strip to x=96. Colour the name with the P1 amber token (P1 is amber everywhere). Use 16px label text and 8px tall bars. Drop the duplicate overhead tag, or drop the strip.

findings.where: bottom-left vitals (armour 60 / hp 100) and f1 controls chip
findings.what: The armour bar is about 20px tall and the hp bar about 34px. They are different sizes and 8px apart. The hp text is oversized, and the hp bar runs off the bottom (y≈1068, 12px from the edge). The bars sit at x=24, not the 96px margin. The 'f1 controls' chip floats at x≈410, unaligned with either bar. The brief says it should sit mid-bottom left folded to one line, and it is faint on a dark fill.
findings.fix: Use one 24px bar height for both, with 8px between them. Set the bottom edge at y=1080−54. Set x=96. Make the label 16px. Put the f1 chip at the same x=96, directly above the bars, with 16px text in tx-2 on --ui-panel.

findings.where: bottom row: 'in pillager's party' chip, air strike panel, weapon bar, ammo card
findings.what: Four panels with different heights, borders and baselines crowd the bottom centre. The 'in pillager's party' chip floats alone with no purpose. The air strike panel is cut short of the weapon bar's width, and its 0% label is tiny. The ammo card is flush at the right edge (x≈1910) with no margin.
findings.fix: Share one baseline at y=1026. Use a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius on every panel. Pull the ammo card in to the 96px margin. Fold the party chip into the top-left keyboard chip or remove it. Align the air strike panel's left edge to the weapon bar.

findings.what: The chip is tucked 10px from the corner, with a green mono-style label. It is off the 5% margin and uses a different green and bold weight than the other chips.
findings.fix: Move it to (96, 54). Use 16px f-cond 600 tx-2 on --ui-panel with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius.

findings.where: right edge 'c 103m' extract chip with arrow
findings.what: The chip is only ~30px from the right edge. The label 'c 103m' is cryptic. The teal arrow sits beside the chip rather than on the screen edge, and the label duplicates the top 'extract 103m' chip.
findings.fix: Keep one distance readout, in the top chip. Make the edge arrow a 24px teal triangle on the safe margin.

findings.where: world-space labels ('crawler m-63', 'player 1', the '10' damage number)
findings.what: The labels are small and overlap the enemy sprite. The '10' damage number sits on the crawler's body. The red '!' floats unattached above the enemy. They are readable but cluttered.
findings.fix: Raise the name label 12px above the sprite. Offset the damage number 16px up with a 1px dark outline. Tie the '!' to the label as a 16px prefix.

findings.what: Eight dim slots with ghost weapon silhouettes at ~25% contrast take up most of the bar and distract from the two armed slots. The digits are tiny at 14px.
findings.fix: Draw empty slots at 40% opacity with no silhouette, only a 1px --ui-line outline. Set slot digits at 16px tx-2. Keep the selected slot's 2px lime border.

v.verdict: The hud is readable and has one clear hero number, the ammo count. The edges are still ragged: the score panel sits flush to the top, the damage number overlaps the enemy tag, and the loose chips share no margin or panel style.

findings.what: The panel is flush to the top edge and has no border. The clock overlaps the sun icon, and the 'you 0 sp' and 'p2 0 sp' lines are tiny. The extract chip also butts against the panel's bottom edge.
findings.fix: Move the panel to y=24. Set padding to 16px, radius to 4px and a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Make the sub-lines 16px in --tx-2. Place the chip 8px below the panel and move the sun icon outside the right padding.

findings.where: enemy tag over the crawler (x 730-830, y 408-495)
findings.what: The '10' damage number sits on the tag's bottom edge and covers the sprite. The red '!' floats unattached above the tag.
findings.fix: Float the damage number 24px above the tag, or hide it while the tag shows. Put the '!' 8px above the tag, inside the same group. Leave 8px of clearance between the tag and the sprite.

findings.what: The dropdown is a third panel style: a thin border, a different fill and a chevron that reads as a system control. It is 20px off the right edge. The 'c 126m' chip repeats the extract distance already shown top-centre. The two share no margin.
findings.fix: Use the --ui-panel fill and a 4px radius on the dropdown. Set its right margin to 96px (5%) and align its top to y=24 with the score panel. Remove the duplicate 'c 126m' chip, or move it into the dropdown. Keep the arrow, but only at the screen edge.

findings.what: The card is 10px from the right edge and 62px from the bottom, so it matches neither the left bars nor the weapon bar. The gun name is 28px, which competes with the 24 hero number.
findings.fix: Inset the card 48px from the right edge. Align its bottom with the weapon bar's bottom, at y=1056. Set the gun name to 20px in --tx-2. Keep the 56px hero number for the ammo count.

findings.what: The chip is jammed into the corner at 10px and uses a green-outlined style no other element has.
findings.fix: Fade it out after 3s, or move it to 24px,24px as a 16px --tx-2 glyph on a --ui-panel chip.

findings.what: The bars run to the bottom edge, with hp at 12px from it. The hp bar is much bolder than the armour bar, so two heavy bars stack. The player 2 plate at y 323 floats alone on the left.
findings.fix: Lift the stack to a 24px bottom margin. Make the two bars the same height, 24px each, with 8px between them. Keep the 56px hero on the hp number only. Align the player 2 plate's left edge to x=24.

findings.where: 'f1 controls' chip (x 410-536, y 922-950) and 'player 2 joined' toast (x 893-1027, y 893-930)
findings.what: The chip sits directly on the weapon bar's top-left corner. The toast sits 20px above the bar, and the two share no baseline. Both are 16px or smaller, and neither has a border.
findings.fix: Set both at 16px with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius. Put the chip 16px above the weapon bar at x=554. Centre the toast 16px above the bar, with no overlap.

findings.what: The bar's bottom is 18px from the screen edge, which is a different margin from the left bars and the ammo card. Empty slots 2, 3 and 5-0 are too dim to read at couch distance.
findings.fix: Set the bottom margin to 24px for the whole bottom row. Raise the empty slots' icons to --tx-2 at 50% opacity, and keep the number labels at 16px.

v.verdict: The HUD is readable but it is still a loose scatter of panels with different edges, fills and margins. Almost none of the earlier layout advice was applied.

findings.where: top-centre score plate (team score / 0 sp / you / p1 / 10:00)
findings.what: The plate is flush against the top edge with no margin. The hero 'sp' number (about 36px) competes with the 10:00 timer, which is the same size. The 'you' and 'p1' lines are tiny and sit off to the side. The extract chip overlaps the plate's bottom edge.
findings.fix: Offset the plate 16px from the top with 16px padding. Set the hero number to 56px f-cond 800. Set the timer to 20px tx-2. Put 'you 0 sp' and 'p1 0 sp' in one 16px row under the hero. Leave 8px between the plate and the extract chip.

findings.where: left 'player 1' strip (x≈14–170, y≈325–358) and the overhead 'player 1' tag
findings.what: The strip floats alone on the left edge at 14px and is not aligned to anything. The name is pale blue, but P1 is amber everywhere. The same name is also drawn over the character, so it appears twice. The bars are 4px thick and hard to read.
findings.fix: Move the strip to x=96 or remove it. Colour the name with the P1 amber token at 16px. Make the bars 8px tall. Drop the overhead tag or the strip, not both.

findings.where: bottom-left vitals (armour 60, hp 100) and the 'f1 controls' chip
findings.what: The two bars are different heights, sit 24px from the edge and are not on the 96px margin. The hp bar is clipped by the screen bottom. The label text is cramped and not centred in the bar. The f1 chip sits at x≈410 and floats over the map, so it is not tied to the bars.
findings.fix: Use one 24px bar height for both, 8px apart, at x=96 with the bottom edge at y=1026. Use 16px labels. Put the f1 chip at x=96 directly above the bars, in 16px tx-2 on --ui-panel.

findings.where: bottom row: party chip, air strike panel, weapon bar, ammo card
findings.what: The four elements have different tops, bottoms, border colours and fills. The party chip floats at y≈911, the air strike panel at 893–946 and the ammo card at 868–1017. The ammo card is 10px from the right edge instead of on the margin. The weapon bar is very close to the bottom edge. The air strike panel overlaps the weapon bar. The 60 / 360 number is hero-size, so it competes with the vitals.
findings.fix: Put every panel on a baseline of y=1026 with a 1px --ui-line-hi border, a 4px radius and the --ui-panel fill. Pull the ammo card in to a 96px right margin. Align the air strike panel's left edge with the weapon bar and leave 16px above the bar. Fold the party chip into the keyboard chip or remove it.

findings.what: The chip is jammed into the corner at (10, 5). It uses a green-tinted bold style that no other panel uses. It looks like debug text.
findings.fix: Move it to (96, 54). Use 16px f-cond 600 tx-2 on --ui-panel with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius.

findings.where: right-edge 'c 128m' marker and the 'the scar 0%' label
findings.what: The 'the scar 0%' label sits under the chip and is partly covered by it. The two are a different size and colour from the extract chip at the top, so the same kind of information looks inconsistent.
findings.fix: Draw both markers with the extract chip's style: 16px teal text on --ui-panel. Put the 0% on a separate line 8px below the chip, and keep them within the 96px margin.

findings.where: in-world name tags (crawler c-51, shield, player 1)
findings.what: The tags use three different box styles (orange outline, plain, dark fill). They are the same size as the HUD labels and add clutter near the action.
findings.fix: Use one tag style: 16px f-cond on --ui-panel at 70% opacity with no outline. Use rarity or danger colour only for the text.

findings.what: The weapon slots are 100px wide and only 2 of 10 are filled. The empty slots are dark silhouettes that add noise. The selected slot's border is amber and the slot is purple, so it does not match the lime selection token.
findings.fix: Dim the empty slots to 30% and shrink them to 56px. Give the selected slot a 2px --acc border and leave the fill as it is.

v.verdict: A clean, consistent settings card with a clear focus row and a good X close. It is let down by a mostly empty detail pane, lime used on non-selected values, tiny row text, and a scroll clip at the bottom.

findings.what: The pane is about 780px wide and 880px tall and holds a title plus a 4-word line. Roughly 90% is empty, so the card looks unfinished and the eye has nothing to land on. The description is 16px muted text, too small and low in contrast for couch reading.
findings.fix: Fill the pane with the current value, the allowed options and a default marker. Or narrow it to about 480px and widen the rows. Set the description in 20px f-body tx-1/tx-2.

findings.what: Lime is used on two non-focused rows to mean 'changed from default'. The guide reserves lime for focus and selected only. These two rows read as a second focus state, competing with the real focused row 'render resolution'.
findings.fix: Mark changed values with a small 6px dot or a '·' tag in tx-2, or use tx-1 with a 3px left tick. Keep lime only on the focused row.

findings.what: Focus is shown only by lime chevrons, a lime value and a faint fill. The row has no left bar and no clear raised fill, unlike the left tab, which has a 3px lime bar. The two focus treatments don't match, and the focus is weak for a pad on a couch.
findings.fix: Give the row a --ui-raised fill, a 3px lime bar on its left edge, and a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Match the tab's treatment exactly.

findings.where: settings rows, tab labels, close hint
findings.what: Row names are about 18px muted grey and tab names are about 17px. The 'esc close' hint is 16px at the bottom right. The type is small and nearly the same weight and colour across the list, so the hierarchy is flat. The 20px body size is not met.
findings.fix: Set row names to 20px f-cond 600 in tx-1 or tx-2 at 4.5:1 or better. Set tabs to 20px. Keep the hint at 16px and raise it to tx-2. Add 8px row padding.

findings.what: The last row ('crosshair size') is cut in half at the panel edge with no fade, and the scrollbar is a thin 6px grey bar with low contrast. It looks like a clipping error.
findings.fix: Add a 32px fade-to-panel mask at the bottom of the scroll area, or snap the scroll to whole rows. Make the scrollbar 8px in --ui-line-hi.

findings.what: 'send play data' sits below an uneven gap (about 88px) with no divider or label. The gap reads as a layout bug, and the tab list takes up a lot of space without carrying a lot of information.
findings.fix: Add a 1px --ui-line divider and keep the gap at 24px. Or move it into the footer next to 'esc close'.

findings.what: A small lime tick sits at the top-left of the card border and floats with no purpose. The 'settings' title is only about 30px and is not clearly larger than the pane title 'render resolution'. The header row is also cramped against the divider.
findings.fix: Remove the stray tick, or run it as a 3px bar the full width of the title. Make the title 32px and 700 weight. The pane title should drop to 24px, or be 32px only if it is the screen's main title. Give the header 56px of height.

findings.what: The chevrons sit about 125px either side of the value, a long way from the row label. The tiny '‹' and '›' glyphs are about 14px. Idle chevrons are white and low-weight and look noisy repeated 17 times.
findings.fix: Show chevrons only on the focused row, or dim them to tx-2. Draw them at 20px in a 40px hit target. Tighten the value column to about 200px wide.

v.verdict: The HUD is readable and mostly lower case, but the controls panel covers a whole left-hand chunk of the screen, there are five competing panel styles and the 12/24 ammo number is the only strong hierarchy cue.

findings.what: The controls list is fully open, about 300x300px, on arrival. The rs-1 order says career raids fold it to one short line, mid-bottom left, and F1 opens it. It dominates the left side, hides the player's flank, and is 20+ rows of explaining text. The 'full list' hint also contradicts the order that it is already the full list.
