findings.fix: Fold it to a single 16px line ('f1 controls') at about x=48, y=1000. Expand only on F1. If the party demo needs it open, make that a separate mode flag.

findings.where: top-left scoreboard 'current pillager bots 3' and top-right 'contracts 0/8'
findings.what: Both are large dark panels with carets, in the corners the style guide reserves for the career HUD (top-right should be a vertical 1x1 list of equal items). They give two competing info blocks plus the controls panel, so three heavy panels sit on the left. The scoreboard repeats cash rows at 14-16px, which is below the 16px floor for anything read, with a tight 18px row pitch.
findings.fix: Collapse the bot list to the 'you' row by default with the caret opening it. Raise rows to 16px with a 24px pitch. Move contracts into the cw-trcol vertical stack with the same panel width and height as its siblings.

findings.what: Panels do not share one language. The controls and scoreboard panels use about 2px radius with a thin border, the ammo card is a larger black block, the weapon slots use gold-ringed tiles, the contracts panel is a pill, and the extract chips (teal) have their own rounded rectangles. The guide asks for a 4px radius, one --ui-panel fill (#16191b) and a 1px --ui-line-hi border. The panels look near-black at a different alpha each, and some have no border.
findings.fix: Standardise all HUD panels: fill #16191b at .88 alpha, 1px #4a5257 border, 4px radius, 16px inner padding. Keep only the focused slot lime.

findings.what: The same distance is drawn twice in teal, and 'c 152m' is a cryptic label. This violates the one-place-per-line rule. The timer 8:55 is only about 30px, below the 56px hero size, and the small icon beside it is unlabelled.
findings.fix: Keep the one top-centre chip and delete 'c 152m' (leave only the edge arrow). Raise the timer to 56px f-cond 800, with the extract chip underneath at 16px.

findings.what: 12 / 24 is the right hero, but the '/ 24' is in orange-amber at the same size as the 12, so two numbers compete. The weapon name, 'b / i backpack' and '4 items $1,710' are 14-16px and weak, and the card mixes right-aligned and left-aligned text. The $1,710 repeats the scoreboard's 'you' row.
findings.fix: Make 12 56px tx-1 and '/ 24' 32px tx-2. Align every line right at a 24px inset. Put 'b / i backpack' and the item count on one 16px tx-2 line and remove the repeated $.

findings.what: Nine slots with grey silhouettes for empty or locked weapons. The idle slots are muddy and barely distinguishable from the dark panel, and the two filled slots use different borders (gold vs blue tint). Number labels are about 12px. The bar sits 20px from the screen edge, inside the 5% margin.
findings.fix: Dim empty slots to 40% and hide their silhouettes. Use one lime 2px border for the active slot only, and put rarity in a 3px bottom bar. Number labels to 16px. Lift the bar to a 54px bottom margin.

findings.what: A saturated mid-green fill with 'hp 100' at about 32px bold on top, at the very screen edge (24px inset). It is the loudest thing in the corner and clashes with the --ok green and with the lime accent. The two round status icons above it (amber, green) are unlabelled and use player colours.
findings.fix: Inset to the 5% margin (54px). Slim the bar to 12px with the number outside at 20px. Use --ok #76b97c for health. Give the status icons a 16px label or remove them.

findings.where: world label 'the long dock cache' (top right of the map)
findings.what: The purple label at about 22px with a drop shadow floats in the world. It is the only purple text in the UI, off-palette (the elite rarity is not meant for place names), and it sits near the contracts panel.
findings.fix: Draw it in tx-1 at 20px f-cond 600 with a 60% scrim chip, or fade it out after 3 s.

v.verdict: This is a clean, consistent settings card with good focus treatment, but it has a few unexplained lime values, a mostly empty detail pane, and some small craft problems that stop it reading as polished.

findings.where: value column, 'half' and 'light' rows (effect intensity, screen shake)
findings.what: Lime is meant to mean 'selected' and focus only. Here it also colours the values 'half' and 'light', which are non-default and not focused, with no legend. Two or three lime values on the screen compete with the real focus row at the top and make the accent read as noise.
findings.fix: Draw all idle values in --tx-1. Use lime only for the focused row's value and arrows. If non-default needs marking, use a 4px --ui-line-hi dot or a 3px left tick instead of the accent.

findings.what: The pane is about 780px wide and 880px tall, and holds a 32px title plus one tiny grey line, 'the world only'. About 90 percent of it is dead space, and it outweighs the list in visual mass. The line is also cryptic: it names no option or consequence. The 'selected' lime top rule makes the empty box the loudest element on the screen.
findings.fix: Narrow the pane to about 420px and give the list the width, or fill it with a current-value readout and the list of choices. Rewrite the description to say what the option does. Set the description at 20px --tx-2, not the roughly 18px it is now.

findings.what: The label sits at far left and the value is centred 500px away, with arrows at x=731 and x=982. The eye has to jump a wide gap, and there is no zebra striping or row highlight to guide it. Every row has the same weight, so you cannot scan to what matters.
findings.fix: Bring the value stepper to about 220px from the label's right edge, or right-align the stepper group at the list's right padding of 24px. Add a --ui-raised fill to the focused row and a 3px lime left bar, as the tab rail already does.

findings.what: The last row is cut off mid-text, with ghosted text at y~990 under the panel edge. The scrollbar is a thin 6px track in a dark colour, almost invisible, and nothing else signals more content.
findings.fix: Fade the bottom 32px of the list to --ui-panel, or snap the scroll to whole rows. Widen the scrollbar thumb to 8px in --ui-line-hi.

findings.what: The chip straddles the card's top border, with a teal outline and teal text that is not in the palette role list (--extract is for extraction only). It looks pasted on and clips the frame line. A lime tick also appears at top-left, x 28-60, y 25, with no apparent purpose.
findings.fix: Move the chip inside the header row, right-aligned beside the X, with a --ui-line-hi border and --tx-2 text at 16px. Remove the stray lime tick. If it is a tab marker, put it on the card's full top edge.

findings.where: left rail, 'saves and tools' / 'send play data'
findings.what: The rail has an unexplained 56px gap before 'send play data'. The tab labels are 20px --tx-2 grey, so they are fairly dim next to the selected tab. Rows are about 64px tall, but the list column's rows are 56px, so the two columns do not share a rhythm.
findings.fix: Make the rail and list rows both 56px. Give the gap a 1px --ui-line divider or remove it. Raise idle tab text to --tx-1 at 80 percent, or keep it at --tx-2 and make sure it clears 4.5:1.

findings.what: The legend is 16px and grey, sitting alone in a 60px footer band, and it duplicates the X. There is no pad equivalent and no hint for left/right to change a value or up/down to move. Someone using a controller gets no help.
findings.fix: Show the live device legend as '< > change   a select   b back', at 16px --tx-2 with the key glyphs in --tx-1. Leave out any sentence, and drop the footer band if the legend fits inside the card padding.

findings.what: The card outer margin is about 25px, not the 5 percent (96px) the guide asks for, and the header title is 32px but sits tight against a hairline at y=100. The 4px radius is there, but the double border from the card plus inner panels makes nested boxes (card, then rail, list and detail each outlined).
findings.fix: Drop the outlines on the rail and list and use the --ui-panel fill alone, keeping one border on the card. Add 16px of padding between the title and the hairline.

v.verdict: A readable raid HUD with a good bottom-right ammo hero, but the open controls panel, the leaderboard and the crowded top row compete with each other. Small type, mixed styles and an unfinished feel hold it at a 2.

findings.what: The full two-column key list is open and dominates the left edge. It is about 300x300 px of keycaps and labels, so it competes with the player and the playfield, and it is not the folded single line the style guide calls for in a career raid. Its 'move/gear/fight/raid' headings are dim and tiny, and 'f1 full list' is the only hint of the rest.
findings.fix: Fold it to one short line at mid-bottom left (about 280x32) and let f1 open it. If it stays open, cut it to 6 rows and set labels at 16px tx-2 on a --ui-panel fill.

findings.what: The heading and the four rows are all about 14-16px at the same weight, with no hierarchy. The row names are cramped at about 18px line pitch, and the panel is crowded close to the wall art. The values show '$' for what looks like a score or standings. It also duplicates information that is already in the HUD.
findings.fix: Set the heading to 16px tx-2 and the rows to 20px, and make 'you' lime. Use a 24px line pitch with 16px padding, and make the chevron a 32px hit target. Check whether these figures are money; if they are score, they must read 'sp'.

findings.where: top-centre, timer plus extract chip (860-1030 x 10-75)
findings.what: The 8:55 timer is about 30px, so it is not the 56px hero. The sun icon in a dark circle sits next to it unlabelled. The teal extract chip below it is tiny, and 'c 152m' repeats it at right. The two extract distances show the same information twice.
findings.fix: Make the timer 56px f-cond 800. Keep one extract readout, the teal chip at 20px, and drop the duplicate 'c 152m' chip or turn it into an edge arrow only.

findings.what: The bar is a wide empty strip that covers the building art. Its text is about 16px, and the chevron sits far from the label. A map-name label ('the long dock cache') in magenta-lilac floats loosely below it. It is the only purple text on screen, it has no panel, and it is partly lost against the wall art.
findings.fix: Shrink the bar to its content (about 200 px) and pad it 16px from the edge. Put the area name on a --ui-panel plate in tx-1, or drop the purple.

findings.where: bottom-left hp bar and status icons (22-430 x 940-1068)
findings.what: The green 'hp 100' fill is flat and bright. Its text is large but sits low and hard against the screen edge, only about 12px from the bottom. The two circular status icons above it (amber and green rings) have no labels, and the amber one is unclear. The hp bar's green is the --ok green and loud against the muted HUD.
findings.fix: Keep the bar to about 24px high, with the 'hp' in 16px label type and 100 as a 32px number. Align it to a 48px margin from the bottom and left, and give the status icons small tooltips or counters.

findings.what: This is the strongest element, but the weapon name 'scav pistol' is about 22px and right-aligned against a left-aligned footer ('b / i backpack' at left, '4 items $1,710' at right). The footer text is about 14px and low in contrast. The '/ 24' is the same weight as the hero 12, so there are two heroes.
findings.fix: Make the '/ 24' 32px and tx-2, keep '12' at 56-72px and bold, and set the footer at 16px with tx-2 (at least 4.5:1).

findings.what: The nine slots are dark and low-contrast, so the empty slots are hard to read. The selected slot's amber border breaks the rule that lime means selected, and the second selected-looking slot (blue gun, slot 4) is tinted differently with no clear rule. The ammo counts at about 14px are tiny.
findings.fix: Use a 2px --acc border on the selected slot only. Raise the empty-slot gun silhouettes to 50% opacity, set the ammo count to 16px, and give slot 4 an owned/equipped marker that is not a competing colour.

findings.what: A tiny 16px device chip sits in the corner with a thin green outline. It reads as a debug label and does not match the other panels' border and fill.
findings.fix: Use the same --ui-panel fill and 1px --ui-line-hi border, or merge it into the controls panel header.

v.verdict: A clean, consistent card with a clear lime focus, but the right pane is still mostly empty, the focused row has no fill or bar, and the list is dim and crops mid-row at the bottom.

findings.what: The pane is about 780px wide and holds a title and a four-word description ('the world only'), so roughly 85% of it is empty. It shows no current value, no options and no default marker. The lime top border makes the empty box the loudest shape on the screen.
findings.fix: Narrow the pane to about 480px and give the rows the freed width. Or fill it with the current value at 56px hero, the option list with the active one marked, and a 'default: full' line at 16px tx-2. Set the description in 20px f-body tx-1. Drop the lime top border for a 1px --ui-line-hi border.

findings.what: Focus is shown only by lime text on the value and arrows. The row has no fill, no left bar and no border. The sidebar tab is treated differently, with a raised fill and a left lime tick. A player on a couch cannot find focus quickly, and the two lists disagree on what 'selected' looks like.
findings.fix: Give the focused row a --ui-raised fill, a 3px lime bar on its left edge, a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a tx-1 name. Keep the lime value and arrows. Use the same treatment on the tab.

findings.what: Row names and tab labels are about 18px in a dim grey, below the 20px body size. The tabs are dim enough that, with no list focus, the active 'display' tab reads as the only highlight. Names and values are far apart (names at x=354, values at x=857), and the dividers carry the eye across the gap.
findings.fix: Set row names and tabs to 20px f-cond 600 in tx-1 for the focused row and tx-2 at 4.5:1 or better for the rest. Raise the row height to 64px, or move the value column in to about x=700. Make the arrows tx-2 so only the focused row's arrows are lime.

findings.where: scroll list, bottom edge and scrollbar
findings.what: The last row ('crosshair size') is clipped mid-glyph at the bottom edge, which looks like a rendering fault. The scrollbar thumb is a thin 6px grey bar that sits against the row dividers. The list starts about 10px lower than the tab column and the detail pane, so the three top edges do not align.
findings.fix: Add a 32px fade-to-panel mask at the bottom of the list, or snap scroll to whole rows. Make the scrollbar 8px in --ui-line-hi with 8px of margin from the dividers. Align the tabs, list and pane to one top edge at y=116.

findings.what: The 'settings' title is about 28px, below the 32px --fs-title. The lime tick at the top-left of the card is a stray 36px stub with no purpose. The close X is a thin light stroke with no hit area. 'esc close' sits alone in a 60px footer at the right.
findings.fix: Set the title to 32px f-cond 700. Remove the stub, or run it as a full 3px bar under the title. Put the X in a 40px square with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a focus state. Set the 'esc close' hint at 16px tx-2, and move it onto the footer's left edge, aligned with the tabs.

findings.what: 'send play data' sits detached below 'saves and tools' with a large gap and no divider or label to explain it. The tab list uses 64px steps while the rest of the column below 'display' sits in dead space, so the left column reads as half-finished.
findings.fix: Add a 1px --ui-line divider above 'send play data' and pin it to the bottom of the column with 16px padding. Or fold it into 'saves and tools'.

findings.what: Values such as 'half' and 'light' do not show whether they differ from the default. Every value is the same white weight, so the column reads as a flat list.
findings.fix: Mark values that differ from the default with a 6px dot in tx-2 to the left of the value, or a '·' tag. Keep lime for the focused row only.

v.verdict: The controls list is now one folded 'f1 controls' line and the ammo card has a proper hero number. The HUD is still uneven: panel styles differ, the ammo card and hp bar are mismatched, and the type is small and cramped.

findings.what: The bot list is open by default. The rows are about 14px with a 18px pitch, and the title ('current pillager bots 3') and the rows have the same weight. The panel sits near the screen edge with a 6px inset, and the '$' amounts crowd the right edge.
findings.fix: Collapse it to the 'you' row by default (the caret already exists). When open, use 16px f-cond 600 rows on a 24px pitch with 16px inner padding. Make the title a 16px tx-2 label. Inset the panel 48px from the screen edge, and use tx-1 for 'you' and tx-2 for the bots.

findings.what: The bar is a flat, saturated green slab with no panel, border or radius, and the 'hp 100' label is oversized. It is a different style from the weapon bar and ammo card. It also sits against the screen edge, 12px from the bottom, and clips the world art.
findings.fix: Put it in a #16191b panel with a 1px #4a5257 border and 4px radius, and inset it 48px from the left and bottom. Make the bar 12px high in --ok, with a 'hp' 16px tx-2 label and a '100' 32px tx-1 number. Align its baseline with the ammo card.

findings.where: HUD panel styling overall (score, contracts, extract chip, 'c 152m', weapon bar, ammo card)
findings.what: Panels do not share one recipe. The score box is flush to the top with square corners and no gap. The contracts panel is flush top-right, the 'c 152m' chip is teal-bordered and rounded, and the slots have a different fill. Insets, radii and fills all differ.
findings.fix: Use one panel recipe: fill #16191b at .88 alpha, 1px #4a5257 border, 4px radius, 16px padding. Inset every panel 24px from the screen edge (the score box currently touches y=0). Keep only the selected slot lime.

findings.what: The extract distance is shown twice, with a chip under the score and a second chip on the right edge. The top chip is clipped under the score panel. This duplicates information, which the one-place rule forbids. The 'c' prefix is cryptic.
findings.fix: Delete the 'c 152m' chip and keep only the edge arrow. Make the top chip a separate 16px teal label 8px below the score panel, not fused to it.

findings.what: The timer '9:55' and 'score' label are close to the same size as '0 sp'. The block has no clear hero, and the 56px hero token is unused. Extract and timer compete for attention.
findings.fix: Make the timer the hero at 56px f-cond 800 tx-1. Put '0 sp' at 20px tx-2 beside the 'score' label as one 16px line. Give the block 16px padding and a 24px top inset.

findings.what: The '12' is good, but the card has a dark fill with no visible border. 'b / i backpack' and '4 items $1,710' are 14px, below the 16px floor, and sit at different insets. The '/ 24' is the same weight as the '12'.
findings.fix: Set the 4px radius with a 1px #4a5257 border. Make the footer 16px tx-2 and right-align it at a 24px inset. Set '/ 24' to 32px tx-2 weight 600. Keep '12' at 56px and anchor the card 24px from the bottom and right.

findings.what: The hint is a 16px label with a key cap, floating on the world at the left of the weapon bar. It is low contrast on blue-grey ground and has no panel. It sits 35px above the bar baseline and is not aligned to anything.
findings.fix: Give it the standard panel recipe, or move it into the left HUD column above the hp panel at x=48. Use a tx-2 label with a tx-1 key cap on a #16191b fill.

findings.what: The empty slots 3 and 5-0 are dim, which is fine, but the bar sits 20px from the bottom edge. The key numerals are 12px and low contrast. Only slots 1 and 4 hold weapons, and slot 4 has a blue tint border that competes with the lime selected slot 1.
findings.fix: Raise the key numerals to 16px tx-2. Keep a 24px bottom inset. Remove the blue border from slot 4 and use --ui-line-hi for unselected slots. Show lime only on the selected slot.

v.verdict: The lime value tint on idle rows is gone and the focused row now reads cleanly, but the detail pane is still a huge empty box, the focused row has no fill or bar, and the keyboard chip and the clipped bottom row are untouched.

findings.what: The pane is about 780px wide and almost completely empty. It holds a title and a 'the world only' line in dim grey at about 18px, which says nothing useful. It takes the width the list needs and makes the screen look unfinished.
findings.fix: Shrink the pane to about 420px and give the list the extra width. Fill the pane with a current-value readout in 56px hero type, plus a short list of the choices with the current one marked. Write a real description at 20px --tx-2, for example 'render the world at full resolution, hud stays sharp'.

findings.what: The focus is carried only by lime text and chevrons. The row has no --ui-raised fill and no left bar, so it is weaker than the tab rail's selected state ('display' has a fill and a lime left bar). The two lists do not follow the same focus rule.
findings.fix: Fill the focused row with --ui-raised. Add a 3px lime bar on its left edge, matching the tab rail. Keep lime on the value and the chevrons.

findings.where: value column (chevrons at x 731 and 982, row labels at x 354)
findings.what: The stepper group sits in the middle of the list, about 380px from the labels, and the row dividers carry a long gap of dead space. Label and value are hard to track across the row from a couch. The value text is also not aligned to the right padding.
findings.fix: Right-align the stepper group at 24px from the list's right edge, with chevrons about 220px apart. Alternatively add a faint hover or focus row fill so the eye can follow across. Make the idle chevrons --tx-2 at 20px.

findings.what: The chip straddles the card's top border, outside the header row. It is teal text on a green-bordered box, a colour that is not in the guide for this role, and it is unrelated to the title and the X. A stray lime tick also sits at the card's top-left (x 28-60, y 25).
findings.fix: Move the chip into the header row, right-aligned just left of the X. Give it a --ui-line-hi border and --tx-2 text at 16px. Remove the top-left tick or extend it into a full-width top rule.

findings.what: The last row is cut off mid-glyph, which looks like a rendering bug. The scrollbar thumb is about 4px wide and dim, so it is easy to miss that the list scrolls.
findings.fix: Fade the bottom 32px of the list to --ui-panel, or snap the scroll to whole rows. Widen the thumb to 8px in --ui-line-hi.

findings.what: The 'send play data' entry sits apart from the other tabs with no divider or label. It looks like a stray item. The rail tab text is about 18px, under the 20px body size.
findings.fix: Add a 1px --ui-line divider above it, or give it the same style as the other tabs and place it at the rail's bottom. Set tab text to 20px f-cond 600.

findings.what: The 'settings' title is 32px, but there is a thick empty band to its right until the X. The bottom 'esc close' legend at 14-16px in dim grey is nearly invisible next to the large X, so there are two close cues with different weights.
findings.fix: Keep the X as the close cue and set the 'esc close' legend at 16px --tx-2, or drop it. Use the freed header space for the keyboard chip.

v.verdict: The raid screen is much calmer: the controls list is folded to one 'f1 controls' line, the top-centre timer and score block is clear, and the weapon bar and ammo card read well. It still has uneven type sizes, small corner chips and a flat hp bar, so it is short of polished.

findings.what: The rows are about 14px and cramped at a ~19px pitch. The heading is the same weight as the names. 'you' is not lime, so your own row does not stand out. The panel hangs at an arbitrary y with no alignment to the top margin. Each name sits far from its figure with no divider or tint.
findings.fix: Use 16px labels on a 24px row pitch with 16px padding. Make the 'you' row lime with a --ui-raised fill. Set the heading to 16px tx-2. Move the panel to x=48, y=48 and make the chevron a 32px hit target.

findings.what: The hp bar is a flat, saturated green slab with a '100' about 32px tall that dwarfs the 'hp' label. It touches the bottom edge, sits about 22px from the left, and has no border or track. It looks like a placeholder and is not tied to the weapon bar or ammo card.
findings.fix: Make the bar 24px high on a --ui-panel track with a 1px --ui-line-hi border, using --ok at low saturation. Align it to a 48px left and bottom margin, matching the ammo card's baseline. Set 'hp' at 16px tx-2 and the number at 32px f-cond 700 in tx-1.

findings.what: The block is welded to the top edge with no top padding. 'sp' and the score are the same 28px weight. The timer is only about 20px and sits above a teal extract chip that is cramped against it. The hero number of the whole HUD is not a hero.
findings.fix: Offset the block 16px from the top. Set the score to 56px f-cond 800 with a 16px tx-2 'sp' suffix. Set the timer to 20px. Leave 8px before the extract chip. Keep a single extract readout.

findings.where: extract readouts: 'extract 152m' chip (903-1017 x 86-112) and 'c 152m' chip (1783-1892 x 470-503)
findings.what: The same distance is shown twice in two places. The right chip is a stray island, and its label 'c' is cryptic. It is also a different size and radius from the top chip, and the arrow glyphs are tiny.
findings.fix: Keep only the top chip. Turn the right one into a bare 24px teal edge arrow with no text, or drop it. If it stays, use 16px f-cond 600 on a --ui-panel fill with a 4px radius.

findings.where: top-right 'contracts 0/8 goals 0/3' bar (1603-1900 x 20-53) and area name 'the long dock cache' (1648-1818 x 140-162)
findings.what: The bar is about 14px text jammed to a 297px strip. Its chevron is a long way from the content, and the bar sits 20px from the top where the other panels use different offsets. The purple area name floats on the map with poor contrast and no plate. It adds a second accent colour, and it is far from the title anchor.
findings.fix: Shrink the bar to its content (about 220px) and put it at x=1872-220, y=48 with 16px padding. Set the text to 16px. Give the area name a --ui-panel plate in tx-1 at 20px, or drop the purple.

findings.where: bottom-left 'f1 controls' hint (435-537 x 929-952) and 'keyboard' tag (10-105 x 6-31)
findings.what: The hint text is about 14px on a thin dark chip that is easy to miss over the blue floor. It sits mid-left but not on a margin. The 'keyboard' tag is top-left in green text on a dark chip, a third style of small chip next to the extract chip and the contracts bar.
findings.fix: Set both at 16px f-cond 600 on a --ui-panel fill with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius. Use a key-cap box for 'f1'. Move the hint to x=48. Move the keyboard tag to the same 48px margin.

findings.what: '12 / 24' is the correct hero at about 56px. The card's footer lines ('b / i backpack', '4 items $1,710') are about 14px and tight to the edges. The card is flush to the right edge at 10px and does not line up with the hotbar's bottom edge or the hp bar.
findings.fix: Pad the card 16px and set the footer lines at 16px tx-2. Set the right and bottom margins to 48px. Match the card's bottom to the hotbar and hp baseline.

findings.where: hotbar (549-1558 x 950-1062) and status icons (24-110 x 940-980)
findings.what: The hotbar is solid and readable, and the lime highlight on the selected slot is correct. Empty slots are dim silhouettes that add clutter, and the slot number labels are tiny, about 11px. The two status icons are cryptic, with an amber and a teal ring, and have no counters.
findings.fix: Hide the empty-slot silhouettes at 0.25 opacity or drop slots 5-9 until filled. Set the slot numbers at 14px minimum. Give the status icons a 16px label or a timer.

v.verdict: a clean, consistent how-to-play card with strong hierarchy and a clear lime action, held back by tiny headers, a stray ghost tag at the top, and a cramped bottom edge.

findings.what: A faint, almost invisible 'keyboard' pill sits at the top edge with very low contrast and no clear purpose. It reads as a rendering leftover, and it is clipped close to the screen edge.
findings.fix: Remove it, or fold it into the card as a device indicator at 16px in tx-2 (#aaa498) with 4.5:1 contrast or better, placed at least 24px from the edge.

findings.what: The headers are about 14px, muted grey and tightly tracked. They are smaller than the key caps and rows beneath them, so the table's structure is the weakest thing on the card. Nothing shows which device is active.
findings.fix: Set to 16px f-cond 600 with +.04em tracking in tx-1 or tx-2. Highlight the active device's column with a --ui-raised fill or a 2px lime underline.

findings.what: The teal ring glyph and 14px muted text are a tiny side-note that is repeated in both columns. It crowds the key cap and sits below the readable minimum.
findings.fix: Use 16px tx-2 text with 8px between the cap and the glyph, or drop the repeat in the controller column. The teal ring stays as the extraction colour.

findings.what: The primary prompt is right-aligned, 20px, under a double rule (the last row divider plus the footer divider). It is lime only in the glyph, with tx-1 text, so it competes weakly with the title. The card's bottom padding is also tighter than its top.
findings.fix: Remove the duplicate divider and add 24px above the prompt. Make the prompt 24px f-cond 700. Match the bottom padding to the 32px used on the left and right.

findings.where: card chrome, title and close button
findings.what: The lime accent tick above the title is a 3px-high, 36px-wide fragment that looks like a clipping artifact. The 48px outlined x button has a thin idle border and competes with the title.
findings.fix: Extend the tick to a deliberate 48px bar, flush with the card's top edge. Reduce the x to a 40px square with a --ui-line-hi border and add a visible pad-focus state.

findings.what: Row labels (move, aim, fire) are 18-20px in a heavy weight and match the key caps in weight. Every cell therefore reads the same, with no entry point apart from the title. The label column is also wide, with a large empty gap before the keyboard column.
findings.fix: Set labels to f-cond 600 in tx-2 and keep the key caps at tx-1 on --ui-raised. Narrow the label column to about 160px and spread the freed space across the device columns.

findings.what: The wordmark at top left is a plain 32px grey word with no logo treatment. The card sits on an almost empty void, so the identity is generic. The card is also much smaller than the 90 percent window the guide asks for.
findings.fix: Use the real logo lockup at the 5% margin. Scale the card up to about 90% of the screen height, or keep it compact and put the extra space into larger rows (64px) for couch reading.

v.verdict: A clean, consistent how-to-play card with a readable keycap table and a clear lime prompt, but it is a small card (about 44% of the screen width) where the guide calls for a near-full-screen centred card, and it has several small craft problems.

findings.what: The card is about 840x730 on a 1920x1080 screen, so it takes up roughly 44% of the width and leaves wide empty void on both sides. The guide's section 0 (Q43) wants a centred card at about 90% of the screen. The 'pillagers' wordmark floats alone at top-left with no relation to the card.
findings.fix: Widen the card to about 90% (1730x970), or if it stays compact, drop the loose wordmark. If the wider card makes the rows too sparse, space the columns at 1/3 each and raise the row height from 56 to 64.

findings.what: A near-invisible dark-on-dark chip at y=19 with barely legible text, so it fails the 4.5:1 contrast floor. It is detached from the card, and it's unclear what it is for (the device indicator?).
findings.fix: Move it into the card header, to the left of the x, as a tx-2 label at 16px with a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Or remove it, since the table already has a 'keyboard' column.

findings.what: The headers are about 14px in muted grey, below the 16px minimum for anything read. They are the only way to tell the two columns apart, but they are the weakest text on the card. The header row also has no top padding against the title, so the first column is cramped under it.
findings.fix: Set them to 16px f-cond 600 +.04em in --tx-2 (#aaa498). Add 8px above the divider. Highlight the active device's column in tx-1 or lime.

findings.what: There are two stacked horizontal rules under the 'loot' row, at y=800 and y=808, which looks like a doubled border. The prompt then sits in a 100px footer with a large gap and no separation from the table.
findings.fix: Remove one rule (the last row's divider). Use a single 1px --ui-line above the footer, with 16px padding on each side.

findings.what: The prompt is right-aligned, 24px type, and has a lime ring icon. It is the primary action, so it is correctly lime-accented. However, it is the same weight as the title, and the filled ring reads like a radio button (a selected state) rather than a key glyph.
findings.fix: Make the prompt 20px f-cond 700 with a keycap-style glyph that shows the actual key or button of the device in use, rather than a radio dot. Drop the dot or make it 12px.

findings.what: The keycaps are bold tx-1 at 18-19px on near-black with a 1px border. They have the same weight as the row labels at the left, so the left column and the keys compete. The chips are tightly padded, and 'r' / 'a' / 'x' are tiny boxes next to 'left stick' and 'hold d-down' (uneven widths).
findings.fix: Make the row labels tx-2 at 20px weight 600 and keep the keycaps tx-1 at 20px. Give the caps a minimum width of 32px and 8px horizontal padding so single letters look like keys.

findings.what: The teal ring glyph plus 'in the ring' text is a unique inline explanation, 14px in grey, and it crowds the cap on the same row. It also repeats on both columns, which is clutter.
findings.fix: Show it once, as a teal 16px label under 'extract' in the row-label column ('in the ring'), and remove the repeats from the key columns. Or put the ring icon only in the label column.

findings.what: The lime tick (about 36px wide) at the top-left of the border is a nice accent. But the 'x' button is a 48px outlined box that sits at a different baseline from the title, and a 56px header row does not centre them (title y=218, x y=216).
findings.fix: Align both to a shared centre line in a 56px header, give the x a 40px square with 1px --ui-line-hi, and show a lime focus ring on it when the pad focuses.

v.verdict: A clean, readable, all-lower-case controls table with a sensible lime prompt, but the card is small for a screen that should fill 90%, and it has a near-invisible tab at the top, a dead row at the bottom and a weak identity.

findings.what: A tiny, dark, low-contrast chip sits at the very top edge. It is almost unreadable and unexplained, and it reads as a stray debug or device label that adds clutter.
findings.fix: Remove it, or fold it into the card as a 16px tx-2 device label. If it must stay, make it 16px, tx-2 (4.5:1 or better) and sit it inside the safe margin (48px from the top).

findings.what: The card is about 838x730 (roughly 44% of the width), which is well short of the settled 'centred card at nearly the entire screen'. About 55% of the screen is empty void, and the 'pillagers' wordmark floats in the top-left, unrelated to the card.
findings.fix: Grow the card to about 90% (1728x972), or at minimum widen it to about 1200px. Scale the rows to 56px and the key chips to 20px, and pull the two columns apart. Anchor the wordmark to the card, or drop it.

findings.what: The chips are 20px bold with a boxed border on every cell. At couch distance this makes about 20 identical little boxes with the same weight as the row names, so the hierarchy is flat. The column headers 'keyboard' and 'controller' are about 14px dim grey, below the 16px minimum for anything read.
findings.fix: Raise the column headers to 16px f-cond 600 in tx-2 (or tx-1). Make the row names tx-2 at 20px. Keep the chips as the brightest element on the row, with a --ui-raised fill and a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Make 'hold x' and 'hold e' share one chip style.

findings.what: The teal ring glyph with a 14px dim caption squeezes into the chip cell. It is misaligned with the chip baseline (the text sits about 2px low) and the caption is too small and too dim.
findings.fix: Set the caption to 16px tx-2 and vertically centre the glyph and caption on the chip with a 12px gap. Alternatively, make it a second line under the chip.

findings.what: A trailing divider sits under the last row, followed by a second rule, which leaves a hairline at the bottom with nothing after it. The footer gap before 'press any key' is uneven (about 45px above, about 50px below).
findings.fix: Delete the extra rule. Use a 24px gap above the prompt and 24px padding below it, on the 8px grid.

findings.what: The lime 36px tab at the top-left of the card border is a small, orphaned tick. It is the only accent on the card apart from the prompt, so lime ends up marking two different jobs.
findings.fix: Either make it a full 3px bar under the title, or remove it. Keep lime for the single primary prompt, since the prompt is the 'selected' action.

findings.what: The prompt is the correct primary action and is legible, but at 24px with a ring icon it is only slightly bigger than the body text, and it sits right-aligned and away from the eye path.
findings.fix: Raise it to the 32px title size in tx-1 with the lime ring, and keep it at the card's bottom-right. Make the whole footer row 72px tall.

findings.what: The close button is a 46px outlined box with a 16px glyph and no focus or lime state. It is fine, but at this size it is hard to hit with a pad and feels weak next to the title.
findings.fix: Make it 48x48 with a 20px glyph and a --ui-line-hi border. Give it a lime 2px outline when focused.

v.verdict: The raid HUD reads clearly, but the easy-mode prompt floats over a live raid with a bare countdown, an empty top half and no scrim, and a lot of small HUD chrome competes with it.

findings.what: The bare '9' is about 16px, dim grey and unlabelled. It is the only time pressure on the prompt and it looks like a stray number. It sits far from the title and the buttons.
findings.fix: Make it a 32px f-cond 700 number in tx-1. Put a 4px lime progress bar along the card's top edge to replace the 56px tick. Right-align it to the same 32px inset as the title. Alternatively, move it inside the 'y yes' button as 'y yes 9'.

findings.what: There is no scrim, so the raid is fully lit around the card. The minimap, ammo box and hotbar all compete with the question for attention, and the prompt blocks the player's view of the action.
findings.fix: Draw a --scrim at rgba(6,7,8,.80) behind the card if the raid pauses. If it does not pause, move the card to the top-left under the feed, at about 480px wide, and drop it to 60% opacity until it gets focus.

findings.what: The card is 748x255. The title is small (about 28px) and sits in the top-left, with about 80px of dead space to its right. The space between the title and the buttons is larger than the space between the buttons and the bottom edge. The card looks unfinished.
findings.fix: Use a 32px f-cond 700 title with 32px padding on all sides. Put 24px between the title and the buttons. Make the buttons 64px high with an 8px gap between them. Use the same value for the bottom padding as for the sides.

findings.what: The lime fill works as the primary action. But 'n no' has a faint border (about 2:1) and no focus state, so pad focus is unclear. The key letters are the same weight as the words, so they do not read as hints.
findings.fix: Set the 'n no' border to --ui-line-hi (#4a5257) at 2px with tx-1 text. Draw the focus state as a 3px lime outline with a 2px offset. Set the key letter 'y' or 'n' in 16px tx-2 or acc-ink at 60% opacity, with 8px before the word. Set the button label to 24px.

findings.what: Eight of the ten slots are dark weapon silhouettes with the same weight as the two owned weapons. Slot numbers are 14px or smaller in low-contrast grey. The pale 'f' badge on slot 6 is unexplained. The bar is wide and busy for a quiet HUD.
findings.fix: Dim empty slots to 35% opacity and drop their silhouettes. Set slot numbers to 16px tx-2. Show the selected slot with a 2px lime border instead of amber, because amber is reserved for P1 and lime means 'selected'. Remove the 'f' badge or give it a label.

findings.where: top-centre score card with the extract chip
findings.what: The 'you 0 sp / p2 0 sp' lines are about 14px and low contrast. The extract chip overlaps the card's bottom edge. The timer '9:57' is smaller than the score, so the hero number is split between two values. Teal is correct for extraction.
findings.fix: Set the sub-lines to 16px tx-2. Put the extract chip fully below the card with an 8px gap. Make the timer the 56px hero or demote it to 20px. Keep the team score at 32px.

findings.what: The bars have three different heights and the labels are in different sizes and positions. 'hp 100' is about 40px and louder than the ammo. The armour and stamina bars use near-identical blues. The bars crowd the bottom-left corner at about 24px from the edges.
findings.fix: Make all three bars 24px high with 8px gaps and 20px labels. Make hp the only tall bar (32px). Use --extract teal for stamina and a clearly different steel blue for armour. Inset the stack 5% from the screen edge (48px left and 54px bottom).

findings.where: 'f1 controls' hint, left, and the minimap and goals panel, right
findings.what: The 'f1 controls' hint floats at 18px with no panel, on top of busy foliage, so contrast is poor. The minimap's collapse caret and the goals row use a different corner style and a different text size from the other panels.
findings.fix: Put the hint on a --ui-panel plate at 85% opacity with 8px padding and a 4px radius, in 16px f-cond. Make the goals row 20px f-cond 600 with 4px corners, the same as the minimap panel. Align both panels' right edges to the same 48px margin.

v.verdict: This is not the controls table the earlier review covered. It is a tiny 960x540 raid HUD frame floating in a black 1920x1080 canvas, so the 'large' HUD size setting is visibly doing nothing, and a 'want easy mode?' prompt sits on top of the action.

findings.what: The game render fills only 960x540 (the centre quarter) of the 1080 canvas, with black on all four sides. Every HUD element is drawn at half size, so the 'large' HUD size cannot be judged and nothing here is readable from a couch.
findings.fix: Render the capture at the full 1920x1080. If this is a letterbox bug, fix the viewport scaling so the canvas fills the screen with 5% margins (96x54px).

findings.where: top-centre score block, 'extract 141m' chip, goals 0/3, 'controls' chip, 'player 2' tag
findings.what: All of this text is about 8-10px on the 1080 canvas. That is below the 14px floor, and the 16px minimum for anything the player reads. The 'you 0 sp / p2 0 sp' lines and the chip text are illegible, and the 'large' setting made no visible difference.
findings.fix: Scale the HUD with the 'large' multiplier. Set the score hero to 56px, extract and goals labels to 16px minimum, and the 'controls' hint to 16px f-cond 600 in tx-2.

findings.what: The prompt has no scrim, so the HUD and the map stay fully lit behind it. The 32px title rule is missing: the title is about 14px. The countdown '9' sits far right with no label, and a lime sliver at the card's top-left looks like a clipped timer bar. The y/n key labels are tiny, and the yes button is a huge lime slab next to a nearly invisible 'no'.
findings.fix: Add a --scrim rgba(6,7,8,.80) layer behind it. Set the title to 32px f-cond 700. Make the countdown a full-width 4px lime bar along the card's top edge. Set button text to 20px with the key shown as a 16px keycap. Give 'no' a 1px --ui-line-hi border and tx-1 text.

findings.what: The bars are three different heights and fills with a 22px lime-green hp bar. The labels are small and overlap the fill, and 'hp 100' is bold white on mid green with weak contrast. There is no clear single hero, and the ammo '25 / 150' competes at bottom right.
findings.fix: Make all three bars the same 12px height and 8px gap. Put 'hp 100' at 20px f-cond 800 in tx-1 on a --ui-panel plate, with labels outside the fills. Keep one hero number on screen (ammo 56px).

findings.what: Nine slots are nearly identical dark tiles with grey icons. Only slot 3 has a thin gold outline, and the 5-slot has a purple fill. The slot numbers are about 7px. The row is wider than the player and sits close to the character sprites, and the selected state uses gold instead of lime.
findings.fix: Draw the selected slot with a 2px --acc border and --ui-raised fill. Show rarity only as a 3px bottom bar. Set the slot numbers to 14px tx-2. Add 16px of space between the bar and the player.

findings.what: The minimap's lower third is empty black, and the goals bar is jammed against the map with a tiny chevron. The panels have no shared border or radius with the other HUD panels.
findings.fix: Crop the map to its content or fill it. Put 8px between the map and the goals strip. Use the same 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius on both.

findings.what: The score card butts against the top of the frame with no margin. The chip overlaps its bottom edge, and the teal arrow floats below it. The clock '9:57' is the same size as the sp figure, so there is no hierarchy.
findings.fix: Offset the card 24px from the top. Put the chip 8px below the card, not overlapping. Make the sp figure the hero at 56px and the clock 20px.

findings.what: There are two 'player 2' tags: a blue bar at left and a cyan tag over the sprite. The left one has two tiny bars with no text hierarchy, and the colour is not consistent with the rule that P2 is cyan.
findings.fix: Use the cyan #47d8c6-family P2 colour for both tags. Set the label to 16px f-cond 600. Set the bars to 8px height with a 1px --ui-line border.

v.verdict: The easy-mode prompt has a clear hierarchy, with a lime yes button, a quiet no button and a flat dark card. It is let down by a stray countdown number, a title that is too small, an overly generous empty gap and a HUD that stays busy behind the modal.

findings.where: modal card, countdown '9' at the right of the title
findings.what: The bare '9' floats in tx-2 grey with no label or ring, so it reads as a stray digit. It is about 16px and sits far from the title.
findings.fix: Make it a 32px f-cond 800 lime number with a small 'sec' label beneath it, or draw a 2px lime ring or bar that drains. Align it to the title baseline, 32px from the right edge.

findings.what: The title is about 28px and sits in the top-left, with a 90px dead gap between it and the buttons. The card feels empty and the question does not command the screen.
findings.fix: Set the title to 32px f-cond 700 tx-1 with 32px padding. Cut the gap to the buttons to 24px and shorten the card height to about 200px. Optionally add a 16px tx-2 sub-label on its own line.

findings.where: scrim and HUD behind the modal
findings.what: There is no scrim. The minimap, ammo, hotbar and team score all stay at full brightness, so the modal competes with the HUD and the busy map shows around its edges.
findings.fix: Add a --scrim rgba(6,7,8,.80) layer behind the card, or at least dim the HUD to 40% while the prompt is up.

findings.what: The key letters 'y' and 'n' share the label weight and size, so the key hint is not set apart. The 'no' button's 1px border is faint (about #3a3f43). Neither button shows a pad-focus state.
findings.fix: Set the key hint to a 16px tx-2 chip with 8px gap to the label. Use --ui-line-hi #4a5257 for the idle border. Give the focused button a 2px lime outline with a 2px offset. Make the labels 20px f-cond 700.

findings.what: The lime tick on the card's top edge is about 55px wide and looks like an accident. The card also has square corners where the style guide asks for a 4px radius.
findings.fix: Extend it to a deliberate 48px by 3px bar flush with the card's top edge, or remove it. Set the card radius to 4px.

findings.where: HUD team score and minimap tag
findings.what: The team score block is about 14px tx-2 with 'you 0 sp / p2 0 sp' crammed beside the 0 sp, and it is cut off by the top edge of the screen. The 'goals 0/3' bar is flush against the minimap. The extract tag overlaps the card's lower edge.
findings.fix: Give the score block 16px minimum text and 16px top padding. Add 8px of spacing under the minimap before the goals row. Keep a 4px gap between the extract tag and the card.

findings.what: The armour, stamina and hp bars are three different heights with different type sizes. The 'hp 100' label is oversized against the others, and the labels are tight against the bar edges.
findings.fix: Use one bar height of 24px and one 16px f-cond 600 label with 8px inside padding. Reserve the 56px hero size for the ammo count only.

v.verdict: The easy-mode card is clean and the lime yes button clearly leads, but the card is oversized for a yes/no, sits on an unscrimmed live HUD, and the surrounding HUD uses mismatched sizes and focus colours.

findings.what: There is no scrim. The card sits over the busy map and hotbar, and the hotbar and HUD stay at full brightness, so they compete with the question.
findings.fix: Add a full-screen scrim at rgba(6,7,8,.80), per the --scrim token, behind the card. Or dim the HUD to about 40% while the prompt is open.

findings.where: countdown '9' at the card's top right
findings.what: A bare 16px grey digit with no label. It is unclear whether it is a timer or a count. It is also the only urgency cue, and it is nearly invisible against the title.
findings.fix: Show it as '9s' at 32px f-cond 700 in tx-1. Or add a 3px lime bar along the card's top edge that drains over the timeout, replacing the 56px stub at top left. Put the digit in --warn for the last 3 seconds.

findings.what: The key letter and the label have the same weight and size, so 'y yes' reads as a stutter. The idle 'no' button is a thin 1px outline that is easy to miss. Pad focus on 'no' is not visible, and the lime fill on 'yes' implies it is the default answer to a difficulty-lowering question.
findings.fix: Draw the key as a 28px square chip with a --ui-line-hi border at the button's left, then the label at 20px f-cond 600. Give the idle button a 2px --ui-line-hi border and a --ui-raised fill. Move the lime fill to whichever button has focus. Default the focus to 'no'.

findings.what: The card is 748x255 with 36px padding and a 160px-tall dead band between the title and the buttons. For two options it feels like a template, not a Halo-style compact prompt.
findings.fix: Use 32px padding on all sides, a 32px gap between the title and the buttons, and 72px-tall buttons. Cut the height to about 200px. Add one 16px tx-2 line under the title stating what easy mode changes, or leave it out.

findings.what: Two different selected treatments appear at once: an amber ring on slot 2 and a blue fill on slot 4. The 'f' chip on slot 4 is also unexplained. Lime means 'selected', and amber is P1's colour, so the two rules conflict. Empty slots are nearly black, so the bar looks like 7 dead boxes.
findings.fix: Give the active slot one 2px ring in --acc. Mark the secondary slot with a 3px bottom bar in its rarity colour. Lift the empty-slot silhouettes to 25% opacity and raise the slot number labels to 16px tx-2.

findings.what: The tag overlaps the panel's bottom edge with no gap. 'you 0 sp / p1 0 sp' is about 13px, below the 16px floor. The weather icon is a floating circle with no panel.
findings.fix: Put 8px of space between the tag and the panel, or dock the tag inside the panel as a third row. Set the sub-scores to 16px tx-2. Align the weather icon to the panel's baseline in the same 4px-radius panel.

findings.what: The three bars have different heights and label sizes. 'hp 100' at about 40px outshouts the compact smg ammo hero at bottom right. The bars have no 8px-grid gap and their labels crowd the fill edges.
findings.fix: Make every bar 24px tall with a 16px label and 8px gaps. Reserve the single 56px hero number for ammo, and set hp to 32px at most. Keep it ok-green.

findings.what: The hint is a small 16px chip floating mid-left, detached from the corner groups, and it half-overlaps a crate sprite. The enemy tag 'crler e-18' reads as a truncated or typo string.
findings.fix: Anchor the hint at the mid-bottom left per the raid-controls order, with 24px from the edge. Fix the label string, or make it a full word such as 'crawler'.

v.verdict: This is a different screen from the one I last reviewed: a mid-raid easy-mode prompt on a HUD rendered at half size, so almost all text falls below the 16px floor, and the prompt is a small card with a lone lime button.

findings.where: whole frame (the 960x540 game render centred in a 1920x1080 black letterbox)
findings.what: The picture is a quarter-area render with black borders. Row names, hints, bar labels and key chips measure about 9-12px. That is below the 16px readable floor and cannot be judged as a couch-readable 1080 screen.
findings.fix: Capture the HUD at a true 1920x1080 and rescale all text to the 20/16px tokens. If the render is deliberately a small window, do not use it as the reference frame.

findings.what: The title is about 14px and the countdown '9' at the right is about 10px, dim and unlabelled. The yes/no labels are about 10px inside 160x40 buttons. The card is a small box in the middle of the play area with a large empty gap under the title. Hierarchy is only the lime fill, and the question does not read as a decision moment.
findings.fix: Make the title 32px f-cond 700 and the button text 20px. Use 56px-tall buttons with 16px gaps. Put the countdown on the right as a 20px tx-2 number with a 'sec' label, or as a thin lime timer bar along the card's top edge. Set the card padding to 32px and make the card about 640px wide.

findings.what: The key chips 'y' and 'n' are plain text in the label, with the same weight and size as the word. Pad focus is only implied by the lime fill. The 'no' button's 1px line-hi border on near-black is faint, so the two buttons are not clearly the same component.
findings.fix: Draw a distinct 20px chip (a --ui-raised fill with a 1px --ui-line-hi border) before each word. Keep 'yes' as the single primary fill. Give 'no' a --ui-raised fill with a 2px --ui-line-hi border and tx-1 text.

findings.what: 'team score' is about 8px. 'you 0 sp / p1 0 sp' is about 9px and crammed to the right of the hero. The panel is clipped flush to the top edge with no margin. The 'extract 148m' tag sits tight under it and nearly touches the panel's lower border.
findings.fix: Set the panel 24px from the top. Make the hero 56px, and make the two sub-scores 16px tx-2 on their own line below. Leave 8px between the panel and the extract tag, and use a 16px teal label.

findings.what: The bars are different heights, and the saturated green hp bar overpowers the ammo hero. The labels sit inside the fills at about 10-12px, and 'armour 40' loses contrast on the blue fill. The block sits about 15px from the edge, off the 5% margin.
findings.fix: Use a uniform 12px bar height with 8px gaps. Set the labels to 16px tx-1 above or left of the bars. Dim the hp fill to --ok at about 80% and leave the numerals as the only bright element. Move the block to a 48px margin.

findings.what: Eight of the nine slots are very dim, with silhouettes at about 25% value. The slot numbers are about 7px, and the lime-ish selection ring on slot 5 competes with the blue slot 1. The bar sits low and close to the player sprites, so the two overlap visually.
findings.fix: Raise the idle slot silhouettes to tx-2 at about 60%. Make the slot numbers 14px. Mark only the active slot with a 2px --acc border. Add 16px of space between the bar and the player.

findings.what: More than half the minimap is an empty black void. The 'goals 0/3' bar is about 10px text with a tiny chevron and a hard-edged box that does not match the other panels.
findings.fix: Crop or fit the map to its content. Use a --ui-panel fill with a 4px radius and a 1px line-hi border. Set 'goals 0/3' at 16px and give the chevron a 24px hit target.

findings.what: The label is about 9px, on a semi-transparent grey chip floating mid-screen with no margin from the foliage. It is hard to read, and it is not clearly anchored to a bottom-left safe area.
findings.fix: Use a 16px label, a --ui-raised fill and a 1px line-hi border. Anchor the chip to a 48px bottom-left margin, aligned with the bar block's left edge.

v.verdict: The prompt is clear and the lime yes button is an obvious primary action, but it is a flat, undersized box dropped on live gameplay with no scrim, an unexplained '9', and loose internal spacing.

findings.what: The card sits on the live game with no scrim. Trees, buildings and the HUD show right up to its edges, so the card doesn't separate from the scene. The card is also only about 39% of the screen width, which is small for a decision the player has to make.
findings.fix: Add the --scrim rgba(6,7,8,.80) behind the card. Use --ui-panel fill with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius. Widen the card to about 880px and centre it on the screen.

findings.what: The 9 is tiny, grey, and has no label or ring, so it is unclear what it counts down to. It is the only time pressure on the screen and it is the weakest element. The accent sliver at the top-left of the card (about 55px wide at y=260) is a timer bar that is too faint to read.
findings.fix: Make the bar a full-width 4px --acc timer across the card top that drains. Show the number as 32px f-cond 700 tx-1 in the title row, with a 16px tx-2 'auto no' caption. Delete whichever of the bar and the number you don't keep.

findings.what: Bold sits in two places: the 32px title and the huge lime fill. The 80px-tall lime slab is much stronger than its 20px label, so the label looks lost inside it. A 60px dead gap sits between the title and the buttons, and the card has no secondary line to explain the choice.
findings.fix: Cut the buttons to 64px tall and set the label at 24px f-cond 700 in --acc-ink. Put 24px between the title and the buttons. Add a one-line 16px tx-2 consequence under the title, such as 'enemies deal less damage', if the choice needs it.

findings.what: The key letter is plain text jammed in front of the word, with a double space, so it reads like a typo ('y  yes'). The player has to guess the first character is a key hint. The no button's label also has low weight and no focus state, so pad focus is not visible.
findings.fix: Draw the key as a 20px chip with a --ui-raised fill and a 1px --ui-line-hi border, 8px left of the label. Label the chips with the pad buttons when a pad is in use. Give the focused button a 2px --acc outline, and give the no button a --ui-raised fill.

findings.what: The title is vertically close to the top edge but about 190px above the bottom, so the card padding is uneven (about 50px above the title, 36px on the sides, 36px below the buttons). The title also feels small for a card this size.
findings.fix: Use equal 32px padding on all sides. Keep the title at 32px f-cond 700 tx-1 and align its baseline with the countdown.

findings.what: The card covers the centre of the play space, the minimap and goals list are still at full strength, and the controls chip and hotbar stay lit. The card competes with an already busy HUD.
findings.fix: While the prompt is open, drop the HUD to 40% opacity. Alternatively, move the card to the lower-third centre, away from the player's view, and keep the scrim.

findings.what: The chip sits tight against the hotbar (a 14px gap) and shows the key as a small dark box. The chip's text is about 16px but lower in contrast than the armour bar beside it.
findings.fix: Add a 16px gap to the hotbar. Set the chip text in tx-2 at 16px with a 1px --ui-line-hi border, and align its baseline with the hotbar top.

v.verdict: The easy-mode card that dominated the last version is gone, and the HUD now reads as a coherent ARC-Raiders-style set of flat dark panels. The hotbar is oversized and its selected slot still uses amber, the left stat bars are crude and crowded, and the type sizes don't follow the scale.

findings.what: The hotbar is the heaviest object on screen. It covers the play area, and nine near-equal slots all have a bright border. The slot numbers are tiny and sit at the slot edge. The selected slot (6) uses a thin amber outline, which you told us to change to lime or P1 amber (the two rules conflict), and it barely stands out from slot 2's green fill.
findings.fix: Shrink the slots to 72px. Drop empty-slot silhouettes to 30% opacity and remove their borders. Use a 3px --acc outline plus an --ui-raised fill on the selected slot only. Set slot numbers to 16px tx-2. Show ammo in 16px f-cond 600.

findings.what: The three bars have different heights, different fonts and different fills (blue, light blue, green). hp is much larger than the other two, so there are three type sizes in one stack. Labels sit tight against the bar edges. The bars use a saturated off-palette colour for every state, and hp 100 as a green slab reads as a debug bar, not Destiny's quiet hero number.
findings.fix: Make all three bars 14px high with a 4px gap. Put the label (16px f-cond 600, tx-1) above or inside the left end and the value right-aligned in the same size. Make hp the only bar with the 32px hero value. Use --ok for hp, a muted blue for armour and tx-2 for stamina. Align the stack to the same 5% margin (96px) as the ammo card.

findings.where: top-centre score panel and extract chip
findings.what: The panel packs the team score (0 sp), the you and p2 lines, the timer and the extract chip into one box. The sizes are all different, the you and p2 lines are cramped and small (about 13px), and the extract chip overlaps the panel's bottom edge. The teal triangle marker floats 40px under the chip with no link to it.
findings.fix: Give the timer the 56px hero slot. Set the team score to 20px and the you and p2 lines to 16px with a 24px column gap. Put the extract chip fully below the panel with an 8px gap and attach the arrow to it, or drop the chip border and use --extract text only.

findings.what: The right side is three different boxes with different widths, border styles and edges. The minimap is wide and has an empty black lower half. The goals row has a chevron the same weight as the minimap's. The ammo card is a different width again and its right edge sits 10px from the screen edge, not on the 5% margin the others use.
findings.fix: Use one column width of 360px and one right margin of 48px for all three. Crop the minimap to its content or fill the void. Use --ui-panel with a 1px --ui-line-hi border everywhere. Make the chevrons 16px tx-2.

findings.what: The weapon name is in a muted grey and is small, the 7 / 42 uses two weights, and the hero number is too close to the card's right and bottom edges, which reads as clipped.
findings.fix: Use 24px padding on every side. Set the name to 20px tx-1 and 7 at 56px f-cond 800 tx-1. Set / 42 at 32px tx-2. Align the right edge to the 48px margin.

findings.where: left player 2 plate and f1 controls chip
findings.what: The player 2 plate floats mid-left with a plain blue label, a thin green bar and a blue bar. The f1 controls chip sits at a different left offset (about 240px) and slightly overlaps the hotbar's area. Neither lines up with the stat stack at the bottom left.
findings.fix: Put the player 2 plate in the left column at x=48px, directly above the hp stack with a 24px gap. Put the f1 controls chip at x=48px, 16px above the bar stack, with a 16px tx-2 label. Give the key f1 a 1px --ui-line-hi box.

findings.where: in-world labels (player 2 tag, shield tag, extract arrow)
findings.what: The player 2 tag has a hard blue fill and a 12px label. The shield tag is a small white chip on a similar-coloured floor, so it is low contrast. The tags don't match the HUD's panel language.
findings.fix: Use one world-tag style: --ui-panel at 85% opacity, 1px border in the player colour (P1 amber, P2 cyan), 16px f-cond 600 tx-1, 8px horizontal padding, radius 4px.

findings.where: weather icon (top, right of the score panel)
findings.what: A lone circular cloud-sun icon sits 20px from the score panel with no label or panel, so it looks like it was left behind. It uses a different shape language (a circle) and a different edge treatment from everything else.
findings.fix: Put it inside the score panel's right edge at 24px, or drop it onto the minimap header row. Use the same 4px radius and --ui-panel fill.

v.verdict: The game frame is still rendered as a 960x540 window in the middle of a 1920x1080 black canvas, so the 'large' HUD size has no visible effect, and the HUD inside it is still tiny and uneven.

findings.what: The capture is a quarter-area picture in a black field. The previous P0 about the viewport was not fixed. The 'large' setting changes nothing, which matches the file name 'hud size row does nothing'.
findings.fix: Render the canvas at the full 1920x1080 with 5% margins (96x54px). Scale the HUD by the size multiplier (large = 1.25x) relative to that 1080 height, not relative to the 540px inner frame.

findings.where: top-centre score block, 'extract 141m' chip, 'goals 0/3', 'controls' hint, 'player 2' tag
findings.what: Text is about 8-10px tall, far below the 16px floor. The score block is clipped at the frame's top edge, with 'team score' at about 7px, '0 sp' at about 14px and 'you 0 sp / p2 0 sp' at about 7px. No hero number reads first.
findings.fix: Set '0 sp' to 56px f-cond 800 and the extract timer to 32px. Set 'team score', 'you', 'p2', 'goals', 'controls' and 'extract' labels to 16px f-cond 600 in tx-2. Move the block 24px down from the top so it is not clipped. Set the extract chip to 16px with 8px padding.

findings.what: The bars still have different heights. The hp bar is about 20px with a saturated green fill and bold lime-white text. The armour and stamina bars are about 11px, with labels crammed inside the fills. hp is the loudest item on screen, which competes with ammo.
findings.fix: Set all three bars to 12px high with an 8px gap. Use --ok for the hp fill. Put the labels outside the bars at 16px f-cond 600 tx-2, and the value at 20px tx-1. Remove the bold 'hp 100' so ammo is the only hero element.

findings.what: The selected slot (5) is only distinguished by a thin amber ring and a purple tint. Slot 3 also has a strong blue fill, so two slots read as selected. Slot numbers are about 6px and ammo counts about 8px. The bar sits 25px above the players with no breathing room.
findings.fix: Draw only the selected slot with a 2px --acc border and --ui-raised fill. Show rarity as a 3px bottom bar, never as a tinted fill. Set the slot numbers to 14px tx-2 and the ammo counts to 16px tx-1. Put 16px of space between the bar and the player.

findings.what: The ammo card is the one correctly sized hero, but it is pressed against the right edge, only about 4px from the frame edge. 'support mg' is about 12px and the card does not align with the minimap above it.
findings.fix: Inset the card 48px from the right and bottom edges. Align its right edge with the minimap's right edge. Set 'support mg' to 16px f-cond 600 tx-2. Keep 60 / 360 at 56px.

findings.what: The minimap is large next to the rest of the HUD, with a dead black lower half. The 'goals 0/3' bar is about 8px text with a chevron, and the panel edges are 4px from the frame edge.
findings.fix: Crop the minimap to its drawn content. Set the 'goals 0/3' text to 16px. Inset the stack 48px from the top-right corner. Use a 1px --ui-line-hi border and --rad 4px.

findings.where: 'player 2' tag at left (488,432 to 582,453) and 'controls' chip (595,584)
findings.what: These two items float without alignment to other HUD elements. 'controls' sits mid-left, not mid-bottom-left as the owner ordered. Both are tiny.
findings.fix: Put the 'controls' chip at the bottom-left, 16px above the hp stack, left-aligned at x=96, with a 16px keycap 'f1'. Set the 'player 2' tag to 16px, left-aligned with the same margin.

v.verdict: This is now an in-raid HUD, not the 'want easy mode?' modal I reviewed before, and it reads as a competent but template-like HUD. The corner clusters are uneven, the top-centre score box is tiny, and the left stats bars are inconsistent with each other.

findings.what: The three bars use three different heights and fill styles. hp is a thick solid green slab with a 40px-plus number, armour and stamina are thin blue bars with 20px labels, and the text sits on a coloured fill with weak contrast. The cluster is also crammed against the bottom-left edge at about 22px, well inside the 5% margin.
findings.fix: Give all three bars the same 20px height, 8px gap and 4px radius on a --ui-panel fill with a 1px --ui-line border. Put the label at 16px f-cond in tx-1 on the left and the number right-aligned. Make hp the only one with a hero-size number (56px, f-cond 800). Move the cluster to 48px from the left and bottom edges.

findings.what: The score ('0 sp') is the hero here but is only about 28px. The 'team score' label (about 12px) and 'you 0 sp / p2 0 sp' (about 13px) are below the 14px floor. The timer 9:57 sits in the same box at a competing size, and the teal 'extract 141m' pill is glued to the bottom edge with no gap, so the box looks like three stacked fragments.
findings.fix: Set the score to 32px f-cond 800 and the timer to 20px. Raise all secondary text to 16px in --tx-2. Put 8px of space between the box and the extract pill, or merge the pill into the box as a bottom row separated by a 1px --ui-line. Pad the box 16px.

findings.what: Nine identical dark tiles, with the digit labels at about 12px and tx-2 grey. The selected slot (5) is marked only by a thin amber/gold outline, which clashes with the lime-is-selected rule and the gold-is-never-a-fill rule. The two filled slots show a small 360 ammo number at 13px that is hard to read from a couch. The empty and unowned slots carry almost the same visual weight as the owned ones.
findings.fix: Draw the selected slot with a 2px --acc outline and a 2px offset. Set slot numbers and ammo counts to 16px f-cond 600. Dim empty slots to 40% opacity. Keep the slot radius at 4px and the gap at 8px.

findings.what: 60 / 360 is clear, but the card is not aligned with the hotbar, whose top is at about y=952 against the card's top at about 903. The 'support mg' label is about 22px and right-aligned, while the left cluster uses left-aligned labels. The card also sits about 10px from the right edge, so the bottom corners are uneven.
findings.fix: Align the card's bottom and right edges to the same 48px margin as the left cluster. Make its height match the hotbar (about 108px). Set the label to 16px tx-2 and the 60 to 56px f-cond 800 tx-1, with '/ 360' at 20px tx-2.

findings.what: The minimap is a plain black rectangle with a collapse chevron overlapping its corner icons, and its edge is flush at about 17px from the top and 18px from the right. The 'goals 0/3' bar is a different style from the score box (lighter border, dropdown chevron), and the 20px label has no hierarchy against the map above it.
findings.fix: Inset both panels 48px from the top and right. Give them the same --ui-panel fill and 1px --ui-line-hi border at 4px radius. Move the collapse chevron out of the map area into the goals header. Set the goals label to 16px f-cond 600.

findings.what: This is the raid controls list from the spec, but it sits at about x=436, floating beside the vitals rather than at mid-bottom left, and the 'f1' keycap is displayed as 'fl' (the font renders 1 like l). Its 16px tx-2 text is low contrast against the busy ground.
findings.fix: Anchor it at the bottom-left, 24px above the hotbar's left edge. Use a tabular 'f1' glyph, 16px f-cond 600 in --tx-1, on a --ui-panel chip with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 8px padding.

findings.where: player 2 name plate (left edge) and in-world tags
findings.what: The 'player 2' panel is jammed against the left edge at about 15px, with a bar that is about 6px tall and a name at about 16px. The in-world 'player 2' and 'shield' tags are about 12px with cyan on a dark chip. They use a different chip style from the HUD panels.
findings.fix: Move the plate to 48px from the left. Give it the 20px name and a 12px-tall bar in cyan (P2). Use a --ui-panel fill with a 4px radius. Set the in-world tags to 14px minimum and the same 4px radius and 1px border.

findings.where: weather icon (top, right of the score box)
findings.what: A small round cloud/sun icon floats alone at the top, with no label, border, or alignment to the score box or the minimap.
findings.fix: Fold it into the score box's right edge as a 20px glyph, separated by a 1px --ui-line. Otherwise remove it.

v.verdict: The easy-mode card from the earlier review is not in this frame, which shows the large-size race HUD. It reads cleanly in the corners, but the oversized 10-slot hotbar dominates the middle of the screen and sits on top of the players.

findings.what: The bar is about 1200px wide with 10 equal slots. Seven are empty dim silhouettes, so it is the heaviest block on screen and it covers the play space directly above the player sprites. It also repeats the ammo count that the bottom-right panel already shows.
findings.fix: Show only owned slots, or shrink empty slots to 48px at 25% opacity. Cut the bar height to about 96px and dock it flush to the bottom margin (32px up). Drop the ammo number from the slot, or drop the panel counter.

findings.what: The active ring is amber/gold, not --acc lime, so the focus colour is wrong. The purple and blue slot fills are two strong colours that compete with it. Slot 6 has a different frame again, a blue fill plus an 'f' chip, so the two owned slots do not match.
findings.fix: Use a 2px --acc ring on the active slot only. Give both owned slots the same --ui-raised fill and mark rarity with a 3px bottom bar. Draw the 'f' key hint as a 20px chip with a --ui-line-hi border on every slot that has a key.

findings.what: The panel is flush against the top edge with no margin. 'team score' is about 14px and 'you 0 sp / p1 0 sp' is about 15px, both under the 16px floor. The timer sits in a tight stack, so the 'extract 148m' pill touches the panel's bottom edge.
findings.fix: Offset the panel 16px from the top. Set the labels to 16px tx-2 and the timer to 32px f-cond 700. Leave 8px between the panel and the extract pill, and give the pill the same 4px radius as the panel.

findings.what: The three bars use different fills, and the hp bar is much taller and brighter than the other two, which are thin. The text is 20-28px and overlaps the fills at uneven sizes. A bright solid green hp bar pulls the eye to the corner at all times.
findings.fix: Make all three bars 20px tall with a 4px gap. Use 16px f-cond labels inside the bar, left-aligned at 8px padding. Dim the hp fill to --ok at about 80% and go to --danger only below 30%.

findings.what: The hint is 14-16px light text on a small dark pill. It floats over foliage at mid-left with low contrast and no alignment to the bottom-left HUD block. The spec says mid-bottom left.
findings.fix: Anchor it at 32px from the left edge directly above the hp stack, with a 16px --tx-2 label and an 'f1' chip. Use a --scrim fill at .80.

findings.what: The label is tiny, about 14px. It looks like truncated or garbled text ('crler'). It is also drawn over the tree line with only a faint pill behind it.
findings.fix: Show the full name, not a clipped one. Use 16px tx-1 on a --scrim pill with 8px padding.

findings.what: The minimap is about 360px tall and nearly half of it is black void. The 'goals 0/3' bar below it has a bold chevron icon that does not match the minimap's top chevron. The minimap sits 20px from the screen edge, while the ammo panel sits 8px from the edge, so the margins differ.
findings.fix: Crop the minimap to its content, at about 260px tall. Use one 32px right and bottom margin for the minimap and ammo panel. Use one 16px chevron style on both.

findings.what: The 'player 1' tag has a floating bar that is not obviously an HP or armour readout. The 'support mg' name is 24px light text on a panel with 1px borders, while the 60 / 360 number is hero size. The slash and the 360 repeat the number in the hotbar.
findings.fix: Remove the second 360 from the hotbar slot. Keep 'support mg' at 16px tx-2 and keep one hero number. Align the right edge of the panel to the 32px margin.

v.verdict: The HUD still sits as a 960x540 window in a black 1920x1080 frame, so every element is tiny and unreadable at couch distance. The element hierarchy is also unchanged: the 'want easy mode?' card is gone, but the top score panel, the bottom-left bars and the ammo card are all still below the token sizes.

findings.where: whole frame: the game render occupies 480-1440 x 270-810 of a 1920x1080 black letterbox
findings.what: The capture is a half-size render with large black margins, so the HUD is judged at half scale. The score text is about 10-14px and the labels about 8px, far below the 16px minimum. A 'hud size' row that does nothing means the large setting is not applied.
findings.fix: Make the large HUD scale apply to the real 1920x1080 frame. Render at full 1080 and scale text to the tokens: 56px hero, 20px body, 16px label. Do not shoot a letterboxed 50% window as the reference.

findings.what: '0 sp' is about 16px, the same weight as its neighbours. 'you 0 sp / p1 0 sp' is about 8px and illegible. The timer 9:57 is the same size as the score, so there is no single hero. The panel is flush to the top edge with no margin and has a dark box that clips against the frame.
findings.fix: Hero '0 sp' at 56px f-cond 800. Timer at 20px tx-2 on the line below. Sub-scores at 16px tx-2 in a row, with p1 in amber and p2 in cyan. Move the panel 24px from the top with 16px padding. Put a 16px teal 'extract 148m' tag 8px under it.

findings.what: The bar heights are inconsistent: armour and stamina are about 10px and hp is about 20px. The labels are about 10px, with 'armour 40' in the bar and 'hp 100' as a heavy lime label on a saturated green fill. The block hugs the screen edge with a margin of about 13px and no spacing system. The saturated green and blue fills compete with the lime accent.
findings.fix: Use a uniform 12px bar height with 8px gaps. Give labels 16px tx-1 left of each bar and numbers in f-cond 600. Set the hp fill to --ok at about 80% opacity so the number is the bright element. Move the block 48px in from the left and bottom edges.

findings.what: Nine slots of equal weight, five of which are dim grey silhouettes. The key numbers 1-9 are about 7px and the ammo counts about 9px. The strip floats mid-screen above the player, covers the ground the player stands on, and has a thin 1px frame. The selected purple slot carries an amber border, a purple weapon and a blue neighbour, so three accents compete and 'selected' does not read as lime.
findings.fix: Show only owned slots at 72px square with 8px gaps, and dim the empty ones to 30%. Put the slot numbers at 16px tx-2. Mark the selected slot with a 3px --acc bottom bar and a --ui-raised fill. Ammo at 16px tx-1. Move the strip down to a 24px bottom margin so it sits clear of the player.
